translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 264

sentences.zh: 【唐紀八十】 起昭陽大淵獻二月，盡閼逢困敦閏月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 80] From the second month of Zhaoyang Dayuanxian through the intercalary month of Efeng Kundun; a little more than one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 80] From the second month of Zhaoyang Dayuanxian through the intercalary month of Efeng Kundun—a span of somewhat more than one year.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝下之上天復三年（

translations.literal: On the weightier annals of Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, and Refined Filial Sage—Tianfu year three (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Superior Annals of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang, Tianfu year three (

sentences.zh: 癸亥，公元九零三年）

translations.literal: Guihai, equivalent to the year 903 CE)
translations.idiomatic: 903 CE, year guiha of the cycle)

sentences.zh: 二月，壬申朔，詔：「比在鳳翔府所除官，一切停。」

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day of the renzi new moon, an edict proclaimed: "All offices conferred at Fengxiang are hereby revoked."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on renzi, the first day of the month, an edict declared: "Every appointment made at Fengxiang is hereby annulled."

sentences.zh: 時宦官盡死，淮河東監軍張承業、幽州監軍張居翰、清海監軍程匡柔、西川監軍魚全禋及致仕嚴遵美，為李克用、劉仁恭、楊行密、王建所匿得全，斬他囚以應詔。

translations.literal: At that time the eunuchs had all been killed; the Huainan east circuit military commissioner Zhang Chengye, the Youzhou military commissioner Zhang Juhan, the Qinghai military commissioner Cheng Kuangrou, the Xichuan military commissioner Yu Quanqin, and the retired Yan Zunmei were hidden and preserved by Li Keyong, Liu Rengong, Yang Xingmi, and Wang Jian; other prisoners were beheaded to comply with the edict.
translations.idiomatic: By then the palace eunuchs were dead. The eastern Huainan commissioner Zhang Chengye, Youzhou commissioner Zhang Juhan, Qinghai commissioner Cheng Kuangrou, Xichuan commissioner Yu Quanqin, and the retired official Yan Zunmei were sheltered by Li Keyong, Liu Rengong, Yang Xingmi, and Wang Jian and thus survived; elsewhere other prisoners were executed to satisfy the decree.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，門下侍郎、同平章事陸扆責授沂王傅、分司。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Councilor Lu Yi was demoted to tutor of the Prince of Yi and assigned to a branch office.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Lu Yi, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Councilor, was stripped of his post and made tutor to the Prince of Yi with duties at a branch office.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京師，賜諸道詔書，獨鳳翔無之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, edicts were bestowed on all circuits, but Fengxiang alone received none.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Chang'an, edicts went out to every circuit—except Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 扆曰：「茂貞罪雖大，然朝廷未與之絕，今獨無詔書，示人不廣。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "Although Maozhen's crimes are grave, the court has not yet broken with him; to withhold an edict alone shows a lack of breadth toward others."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi said, "Li Maozhen's crimes are serious, yet the court has not severed ties with him. To send no edict to him alone makes us look narrow-minded."

sentences.zh: 崔胤怒，奏貶之。

translations.literal: Cui Yin was enraged and memorialized for his demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin was furious and had him demoted by memorial.

sentences.zh: 宮人宋柔等十一人皆韓全誨所獻，及僧、道士與宦官親厚者二十餘人，並送京兆杖殺。

translations.literal: The palace women Song Rou and ten others had all been presented by Han Quanhui, and more than twenty monks, Daoist priests, and those close to the eunuchs were all sent to the Jingzhao authorities and beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven palace women including Song Rou, all gifts from Han Quanhui, and more than twenty monks, Daoists, and others who had been intimate with the eunuchs were handed to the Jingzhao magistrate and clubbed to death.

sentences.zh: 上謂韓偓曰：「崔胤雖盡忠，然比卿頗用機數。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Han Wo: "Although Cui Yin is utterly loyal, compared with you he relies rather heavily on stratagems."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Han Wo, "Cui Yin is loyal enough, but beside you he leans too much on trickery."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「凡為天下者，萬國皆屬之耳目，安可以機數欺之！

translations.literal: He replied: "Whoever holds the realm—all the myriad states are his eyes and ears; how can one deceive them with stratagems!
translations.idiomatic: Han Wo answered, "Whoever rules the realm has the whole world watching. How can you fool it with schemes?

sentences.zh: 莫若推誠直致，雖日計之不足，而歲計之有餘也。」

translations.literal: Better to extend sincerity and straightforwardness; though daily reckoning may fall short, yearly reckoning will have surplus."
translations.idiomatic: Better to lead with plain sincerity: what falls short day by day will still leave you ahead year by year."

sentences.zh: 丙子，工部侍郎、同平章事蘇檢，吏部侍郎盧光啟，並賜自盡。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Vice Minister of Works and Associate Chief Councilor Su Jian and Vice Minister of Personnel Lu Guangqi were both ordered to take their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Su Jian, Vice Minister of Works and Associate Chief Councilor, and Lu Guangqi, Vice Minister of Personnel, were both commanded to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以中書侍郎、同平章事王溥為太子賓客、分司，皆崔胤所惡也。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Councilor Wang Pu was made Crown Prince's guest of honor with branch-office duties—all men Cui Yin detested.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Wang Pu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Councilor, was made an honorary attendant to the crown prince at a branch post—another of Cui Yin's enemies.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，賜朱全忠號回天再造竭忠守正功臣，賜其僚佐敬翔等號迎鑾協贊功臣，諸將朱友寧等號迎鑾果毅功臣，都頭以下號四鎮靜難功臣。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Zhu Quanzhong was granted the title Meritous Subject Who Turns Back Heaven and Recreates, Exhausting Loyalty and Upholding Rectitude; his aides Jing Xiang and others were granted the title Meritous Subjects Who Welcome the Imperial Carriage and Assist in Praise; the generals Zhu Youning and others were granted the title Meritous Subjects Who Welcome the Carriage with Firm Resolve; commanders and below were granted the title Meritous Subjects Who Pacify Disturbance in the Four Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Zhu Quanzhong received the honorific "Meritous Subject Who Turns Back Heaven and Recreates, Exhausting Loyalty and Upholding Rectitude"; his staff, including Jing Xiang, were named "Meritous Subjects Who Welcome the Imperial Carriage and Assist in Praise"; generals such as Zhu Youning became "Meritous Subjects Who Welcome the Carriage with Firm Resolve"; and commanders down the ranks received "Meritous Subjects Who Pacify Disturbance in the Four Circuits."

sentences.zh: 上議褒崇全忠，欲以皇子為諸道兵馬元帥，以全忠副之。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed honoring Quanzhong and wished to appoint an imperial prince as commander-in-chief of all circuits' armies and horses, with Quanzhong as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated how to reward Zhu Quanzhong and planned to name an imperial prince commander-in-chief of all military circuits, with Zhu as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 崔胤請以輝王祚為之，上曰：「濮王長。」

translations.literal: Cui Yin requested that Prince Hui, Zuo, be appointed; the emperor said: "Prince Pu is the elder."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin urged appointing Prince Hui, Li Zuo. The emperor said, "Prince Pu is the elder brother."

sentences.zh: 胤承全忠密旨，利祚沖幼，固請之。

translations.literal: Yin, carrying out Quanzhong's secret instruction, favored Zuo for his youth and pressed the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on Zhu Quanzhong's private orders, Yin favored the young and pliable Zuo and insisted on him.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以祚為諸道兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: On jimao, Zuo was appointed commander-in-chief of all circuits' armies and horses.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Li Zuo was named commander-in-chief of all military circuits.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，加全忠守太尉，充副元帥，進爵梁王。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Quanzhong was further appointed Grand Preceptor, made deputy commander-in-chief, and advanced to Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Zhu Quanzhong was made Grand Preceptor, confirmed as deputy commander-in-chief, and raised to Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 以胤為司徒兼侍中。

translations.literal: Yin was made Minister of Education and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin was appointed Minister of Education and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 胤恃全忠之勢，專權自恣，天子動靜皆稟之。

translations.literal: Yin relied on Quanzhong's power, monopolized authority and indulged himself at will, and the emperor's every movement was reported to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin leaned on Zhu Quanzhong's might, ruled as he pleased, and even the emperor's comings and goings required his approval.

sentences.zh: 朝臣從上幸鳳翔者，凡貶逐三十餘人。

translations.literal: Among court officials who had accompanied the emperor to Fengxiang, more than thirty were demoted and banished in all.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty courtiers who had followed the emperor to Fengxiang were demoted or driven out.

sentences.zh: 刑賞系其愛憎，中外畏之，重足一跡。

translations.literal: Punishments and rewards hung on his likes and dislikes; inside and outside the court feared him, treading as if on overlapping feet with a single footprint.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments followed his whims; the whole court feared him and walked as if on eggshells.

sentences.zh: 以敬翔守太府卿，朱友寧領寧遠節度使。

translations.literal: Jing Xiang was made acting Director of the Imperial Storehouse; Zhu Youning was put in charge of the Ningyuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang was named acting Director of the Imperial Storehouse, and Zhu Youning took command of the Ningyuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 全忠表苻道昭同平章事，充天雄節度使，遣兵援送之秦州，不得至而還。

translations.literal: Quanzhong memorialized Fu Daozhao as Associate Chief Councilor and appointed him military commissioner of Tianxiong; troops were sent to escort him to Qinzhou, but he could not arrive and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong recommended Fu Daozhao for Associate Chief Councilor and Tianxiong military commissioner, sent troops to escort him toward Qinzhou, and turned back when they could not get through.

sentences.zh: 初，翰林學士承旨韓偓之登進士第也，御史大夫趙崇知貢舉。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Han Wo, Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy, passed the jinshi examination, the Censor-in-Chief Zhao Chong was director of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Han Wo of the Hanlin Academy passed the jinshi examination, Zhao Chong, Censor-in-Chief, had overseen the civil service exams.

sentences.zh: 上返自鳳翔，欲用偓為相，偓薦崇及兵部侍郎王贊自代。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Fengxiang, he wished to make Wo chief councilor; Wo recommended Chong and Vice Minister of War Wang Zan to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from Fengxiang, the emperor wanted Han Wo as chief councilor; Wo nominated Zhao Chong and Vice Minister of War Wang Zan in his place.

sentences.zh: 上欲從之，崔胤惡其分己權，使朱全忠入爭之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to agree, but Cui Yin hated them for dividing his power and had Zhu Quanzhong enter the palace to argue against it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was inclined to agree, but Cui Yin resented losing power and sent Zhu Quanzhong to the palace to object.

sentences.zh: 全忠見上曰：「趙崇輕薄之魁，王贊無才用，韓偓何得妄薦為相！」

translations.literal: Quanzhong saw the emperor and said: "Zhao Chong is the ringleader of the frivolous; Wang Zan has no talent or ability—how can Han Wo presumptuously recommend them as chief councilors!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong told the emperor, "Zhao Chong leads the frivolous set, Wang Zan has no ability—how dare Han Wo recommend them for the chancellorship!"

sentences.zh: 上見全忠怒甚，不得已，癸未，貶偓濮州司馬。

translations.literal: Seeing Quanzhong extremely angry, the emperor had no choice; on guiwei, Wo was demoted to military adjutant of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Zhu Quanzhong's fury, the emperor gave way; on guiwei, Han Wo was demoted to military adjutant at Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 上密與偓泣別，偓曰：「吻人非復前來之比，臣得遠貶及死乃幸耳，不忍見篡弒之辱！」

translations.literal: The emperor secretly wept in parting with Wo; Wo said: "That rebel is no longer what he was before; for your servant to be banished far away and die is fortune enough—I cannot bear to witness the shame of usurpation and regicide!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept with him in private. Han Wo said, "That rebel is not the man he once was. Exile and death would be mercy—I cannot stay to watch the throne usurped and the Son of Heaven murdered."

sentences.zh: 己丑，上令朱全忠與李茂貞書，取平原公主。

translations.literal: On jichou, the emperor ordered Zhu Quanzhong to write to Li Maozhen to recover Princess Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, the emperor had Zhu Quanzhong demand Princess Pingyuan back from Li Maozhen in writing.

sentences.zh: 茂貞不敢違，遽歸之。

translations.literal: Maozhen dared not disobey and promptly returned her.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen did not dare refuse and sent her back at once.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以朱友裕為鎮國節度使。

translations.literal: On renchen, Zhu Youyu was appointed military commissioner of Zhenguo.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Zhu Youyu was made military commissioner of Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 乙未，全忠奏留步騎萬人於故兩軍，以朱友倫為左軍宿衛都指揮使，又以汴將張廷范為宮苑使，王殷為皇城使，蔣玄暉充街使。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Quanzhong memorialized to leave ten thousand infantry and cavalry at the former Left and Right Armies; Zhu Youlun was made overall commander of the Left Army palace guard; and further the Bianzhou generals Zhang Tingfan as palace parks commissioner, Wang Yin as imperial city commissioner, and Jiang Xuanhui as street commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Zhu Quanzhong asked to leave ten thousand foot and horse troops with the former Left and Right Armies, named Zhu Youlun commander of the Left Army palace guard, and installed his Bianzhou men—Zhang Tingfan as palace parks commissioner, Wang Yin as imperial city commissioner, and Jiang Xuanhui as street commissioner.

sentences.zh: 於是全忠之黨布列遍於禁衛及京輔。

translations.literal: Thereupon Quanzhong's faction was deployed throughout the palace guards and the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong's men now filled the palace guards and the capital districts.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，全忠辭歸鎮，留宴壽春殿，又餞之於延喜樓。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Quanzhong took leave to return to his command; a farewell banquet was held at Shouchun Hall, and he was again entertained at Yanxi Tower.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Zhu Quanzhong bid farewell to return to his base; the court feasted him at Shouchun Hall and again at Yanxi Tower.

sentences.zh: 上臨軒泣別，令於樓前上馬。

translations.literal: The emperor came to the balustrade weeping in farewell and ordered him to mount before the tower.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to the balcony in tears and had him mount his horse below the tower.

sentences.zh: 上又賜全忠詩，全忠亦和進；

translations.literal: The emperor also bestowed poems on Quanzhong, and Quanzhong likewise presented matching verses;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Zhu Quanzhong poems, and Zhu returned verses in reply;

sentences.zh: 又賜《楊柳枝辭》五首。

translations.literal: he also bestowed five pieces of "Willow Branch Lyrics."
translations.idiomatic: and also five poems titled "Willow Branch Lyrics."

sentences.zh: 百官班辭於長樂驛。

translations.literal: The hundred officials took their turns in farewell at Changle Post.
translations.idiomatic: The officials lined up to bid farewell at Changle Post.

sentences.zh: 崔胤獨送至霸橋，自置餞席，夜二鼓，胤始還入城。

translations.literal: Cui Yin alone escorted him to Ba Bridge, set out a farewell feast himself, and only at the second watch of the night did Yin return to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin alone escorted him to Ba Bridge, hosted a parting feast, and did not return to the city until the second watch.

sentences.zh: 上復召對，問以全忠安否，置酒奏樂，至四鼓乃罷。

translations.literal: The emperor again summoned him for audience, asking whether Quanzhong was safe; wine was set out and music played until the fourth watch before it ended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yin again, asked whether Zhu Quanzhong had traveled safely, and kept wine and music going until the fourth watch.

sentences.zh: 以清海節度使裴樞為門下侍郎、同平章事，朱全忠薦之矣。

translations.literal: Pei Shu, military commissioner of Qinghai, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Councilor—Quanzhong had recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu, military commissioner of Qinghai, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Councilor on Zhu Quanzhong's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 李克用使者還晉陽，言崔胤之橫，克用曰：「胤為人臣，外倚賊勢，內脅其君，既執朝政，又握兵權。

translations.literal: Li Keyong's envoy returned to Jinyang and spoke of Cui Yin's arrogance; Keyong said: "Yin is a subject who outwardly relies on the rebel's power and inwardly threatens his sovereign—he already holds court governance and also grasps military authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong's envoy reached Jinyang and reported Cui Yin's arrogance, Keyong said, "Yin is a subject who leans on the rebel's power abroad and bullies his sovereign at home—he runs the government and holds the armies.

sentences.zh: 權重則怨多，勢侔則釁生，破家亡國，在眼中矣。」

translations.literal: When authority is heavy, resentments multiply; when power is equal, quarrels arise—ruined families and perished states are before one's eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Heavy power breeds resentment; matched strength breeds strife—ruin of house and state is plain to see."

sentences.zh: 朱全忠將行，奏：「克用於臣，本無大嫌，乞厚加寵澤，遣大臣撫慰；

translations.literal: As Zhu Quanzhong was about to depart, he memorialized: "Keyong and your servant originally have no great enmity; I beg that he be richly favored and that a high minister be sent to console him;
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, Zhu Quanzhong memorialized, "Li Keyong and I have no deep feud. Please honor him generously and send a senior minister to reassure him;

sentences.zh: 俾知臣意。」

translations.literal: so that he may know your servant's intent."
translations.idiomatic: so he may know my intentions."

sentences.zh: 進奏吏以白克用，克用笑曰：「賊欲有事淄青，畏吾掎其後耳！」

translations.literal: The memorial courier reported this to Keyong; Keyong laughed and said: "The rebel wishes to act against Ziqing and fears that I will seize him from behind!"
translations.idiomatic: When the courier told Keyong, he laughed and said, "The rebel means to strike Ziqing and fears I'll hit him from behind!"

sentences.zh: 三月，戊午，朱全忠至大梁。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuwu, Zhu Quanzhong reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuwu, Zhu Quanzhong arrived at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 王師範弟師魯圍齊州，朱友寧引兵擊走之。

translations.literal: Wang Shifan's younger brother Shilu besieged Qizhou; Zhu Youning led troops and struck, driving him off.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan's brother Shilu besieged Qizhou; Zhu Youning drove him off.

sentences.zh: 師範遣兵益劉鄩軍，友寧擊取之。

translations.literal: Shifan sent troops to reinforce Liu Yun's army; Youning attacked and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan sent reinforcements to Liu Yun; Youning intercepted and seized them.

sentences.zh: 由是兗州援絕，葛從周引兵圍之。

translations.literal: Thereby Yanzhou's relief was cut off, and Ge Congzhou led troops to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou's lifeline was cut; Ge Congzhou laid siege.

sentences.zh: 友寧進攻青州；

translations.literal: Youning advanced to attack Qingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Youning pressed the attack on Qingzhou;

sentences.zh: 戊辰，全忠引四鎮及魏博兵十萬繼之。

translations.literal: on wuchen, Quanzhong led one hundred thousand troops from the four circuits and Weibo in support.
translations.idiomatic: on wuchen, Zhu Quanzhong followed with a hundred thousand men from his four circuits and Weibo.

sentences.zh: 淮南將李神福圍鄂州，望城中積荻，謂監軍尹建峰曰：「今夕為公焚之。」

translations.literal: The Huainan general Li Shenfu besieged Ezhou; seeing the reed stacks piled in the city, he said to the military commissioner Yin Jianfeng: "Tonight I shall burn them for you."
translations.idiomatic: Huainan general Li Shenfu besieged Ezhou. Seeing reed stacks in the city, he told commissioner Yin Jianfeng, "I will burn them for you tonight."

sentences.zh: 建峰未之信。

translations.literal: Jianfeng did not believe him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin did not believe him.

sentences.zh: 時杜洪求救於朱全忠，神福遣部將秦皋乘輕舟至灄口，舉火炬於樹杪。

translations.literal: At that time Du Hong was begging Zhu Quanzhong for rescue; Shenfu sent his subordinate general Qin Gao in a light boat to Zhuankou and raised torches in the treetops.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong had appealed to Zhu Quanzhong for help. Shenfu sent Qin Gao in a light boat to Zhuankou and lit torches in the treetops.

sentences.zh: 洪以為救兵至，果焚獲以應之。

translations.literal: Hong thought relief troops had arrived and indeed burned the reeds in response.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong took it for arriving relief and burned the reeds in reply.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己卯，以朱全忠判元帥府事。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jimao, Zhu Quanzhong was put in charge of the commander-in-chief's office.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jimao, Zhu Quanzhong was placed in charge of the commander-in-chief's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 知溫州事丁章為木工李彥所殺，其將張惠據溫州。

translations.literal: Ding Zhang, who held Wenzhou affairs, was killed by the carpenter Li Yan; his general Zhang Hui seized Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Zhang, who governed Wenzhou, was murdered by the carpenter Li Yan; his officer Zhang Hui took Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 王師範求救於淮南，乙未，楊行密遣其將王茂章以步騎七千救之，又遣別將將兵數萬攻宿州。

translations.literal: Wang Shifan begged Huainan for rescue; on yiwei, Yang Xingmi sent his general Wang Maozhang with seven thousand infantry and cavalry to save him, and also sent another general with tens of thousands of troops to attack Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan appealed to Huainan; on yiwei, Yang Xingmi sent Wang Maozhang with seven thousand foot and horse to relieve him and another commander with tens of thousands against Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣其將康懷英救宿州，淮南兵遁去。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent his general Kang Huaiying to rescue Suzhou, and the Huainan troops fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Kang Huaiying to relieve Suzhou, and the Huainan army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 楊行密遣使詣馬殷，言朱全忠跋扈，請殷絕之，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent an envoy to Ma Yin, saying Zhu Quanzhong was overbearing and asking Yin to break with him and covenant as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent envoys to Ma Yin, denouncing Zhu Quanzhong's arrogance and urging Yin to break with him and ally as sworn brothers.

sentences.zh: 湖南大將許德勳曰：「全忠雖無道，然挾天子以令諸侯，明公素奉王室，不可輕絕也。」

translations.literal: The Hunan great general Xu Dexun said: "Although Quanzhong is without the Way, he yet holds the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords; my lord has always served the royal house and must not lightly break away."
translations.idiomatic: Hunan general Xu Dexun said, "Zhu Quanzhong may be lawless, but he holds the emperor hostage to command the lords. You have always served the dynasty—do not break with him lightly."

sentences.zh: 殷從之。

translations.literal: Yin followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin agreed.

sentences.zh: 杜洪求救於朱全忠，全忠遣其將韓勍將萬人屯灄口，遣使語荊南節度使成汭、武安節度使馬殷、武貞節度使雷彥威，令出兵救洪。

translations.literal: Du Hong begged Zhu Quanzhong for rescue; Quanzhong sent his general Han Qin with ten thousand men to camp at Zhuankou and dispatched envoys to tell the Jingnan military commissioner Cheng Ru, the Wu'an military commissioner Ma Yin, and the Wuzhen military commissioner Lei Yanwei to raise troops to save Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong appealed to Zhu Quanzhong, who sent Han Qin with ten thousand men to Zhuankou and ordered Cheng Ru of Jingnan, Ma Yin of Wu'an, and Lei Yanwei of Wuzhen to march to Hong's relief.

sentences.zh: 汭畏全忠之強，且欲侵江、淮之地以自廣，發舟師十萬，沿江東下。

translations.literal: Ru feared Quanzhong's strength and also wished to invade the Jiang and Huai regions to expand himself; he launched one hundred thousand naval troops downstream along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ru feared Zhu Quanzhong and hoped to seize Jiang-Huai territory for himself, so he sent a hundred thousand sailors down the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 汭作巨艦，三年而成，制度如府署，謂之「和州載」，其餘謂之「齊山」、「截海」、「劈浪」之類甚眾。

translations.literal: Ru built giant warships that took three years to complete, with arrangements like government offices; they were called "Hezhou Carriers," and the rest were called "Qishan," "Jiehai," "Pilang," and the like in great number.
translations.idiomatic: He built giant warships over three years, fitted out like government halls—the flagship was called "Hezhou Carrier"—and many others named "Qishan," "Sea-Cutter," "Wave-Splitter," and the like.

sentences.zh: 掌書記李珽諫曰：「今每艦載甲士千人，稻米倍之，緩急不可動也。

translations.literal: Chief secretary Li Ting remonstrated: "Now each ship carries a thousand armored soldiers and twice that in rice—in urgency or calm it cannot be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Chief secretary Li Ting warned, "Each ship now carries a thousand armored men and twice that in grain—they cannot maneuver quickly or slowly.

sentences.zh: 吳兵剽輕，難與角逐；

translations.literal: Wu troops are swift and light—hard to contend with in rivalry;
translations.idiomatic: Wu troops are fast and light—hard to match in battle;

sentences.zh: 武陵、長沙，皆吾仇也；

translations.literal: Wuling and Changsha are both our enemies;
translations.idiomatic: Wuling and Changsha are both our enemies;

sentences.zh: 豈得不為反顧之慮乎！

translations.literal: how can we fail to consider looking back over our shoulders!
translations.idiomatic: should we not fear an attack from behind?

sentences.zh: 不若遣驍將屯巴陵，大軍與之對岸，堅壁勿戰，不過一月，吳兵食盡自遁，鄂圍解矣。」

translations.literal: Better to send fierce generals to camp at Baling, with the main army facing them on the opposite bank, holding walls and not fighting—in less than a month the Wu troops' food will be exhausted and they will flee of themselves, and the siege of E will be lifted."
translations.idiomatic: Better post crack troops at Baling and hold the far bank with the main fleet behind walls. Within a month the Wu army will run out of food and withdraw, and the siege of Ezhou will lift."

sentences.zh: 汭不聽。

translations.literal: Ru would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ru refused.

sentences.zh: 珽，澄之五世孫也。

translations.literal: Ting was a fifth-generation descendant of Li Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting was a fifth-generation descendant of Li Cheng.

sentences.zh: 王建出兵攻秦、隴，乘李茂貞之弱也，遣判官韋莊入貢，亦修好於朱全忠。

translations.literal: Wang Jian sent troops to attack Qin and Long, taking advantage of Li Maozhen's weakness; he dispatched his aide Wei Zhuang to present tribute and also made peace with Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian attacked Qin and Long while Li Maozhen was weak, sent Wei Zhuang to court with tribute, and also courted Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣押牙王殷報聘，建與之宴。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent his guard officer Wang Yin on a return visit; Jian feasted with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent guard officer Wang Yin on a return mission; Wang Jian entertained him.

sentences.zh: 殷言：「蜀甲兵誠多，但乏馬耳。」

translations.literal: Yin said: "Shu's armored soldiers are indeed many, but they lack horses, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin remarked, "Shu has plenty of infantry, but few horses."

sentences.zh: 建作色曰：「當道江山險阻，騎兵無所施。

translations.literal: Jian changed expression and said: "Along our route rivers and mountains are perilous—cavalry has nowhere to deploy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian's face darkened. "Our country is all mountains and rivers—cavalry is useless here.

sentences.zh: 然馬亦不乏，押牙少留，當共閱之。」

translations.literal: Yet horses are not lacking either; guard officer, stay a little, and we shall review them together."
translations.idiomatic: But we are not short of horses either. Stay a while and we will review them together."

sentences.zh: 乃集諸州馬，大閱於星宿山，官馬八千，私馬四千，部隊甚整。

translations.literal: He then gathered horses from all prefectures and held a great review at Xingxiu Mountain—eight thousand government horses, four thousand private horses, with formations very orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He then assembled horses from every prefecture and held a grand review at Xingxiu Mountain—eight thousand government mounts and four thousand private ones, all in tight formation.

sentences.zh: 殷歎服。

translations.literal: Yin sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin was impressed.

sentences.zh: 建本騎將，故得蜀之後，於文、黎、維、茂州市胡馬，十年之間，遂及茲數。

translations.literal: Jian had originally been a cavalry commander; after gaining Shu, over ten years he purchased Hu horses in the Wen, Li, Wei, and Mao prefectures until he reached this number.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian had been a cavalry officer; after taking Shu he spent ten years buying frontier horses in Wen, Li, Wei, and Mao until he reached this strength.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁未，李克用雲州都將王敬暉殺刺史劉再立，叛降劉仁恭。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingwei, Li Keyong's Yunzhou commander Wang Jinghui killed the prefect Liu Zaili and rebelled, surrendering to Liu Rengong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingwei, Li Keyong's Yunzhou commander Wang Jinghui killed prefect Liu Zaili and defected to Liu Rengong.

sentences.zh: 克用遣李嗣昭、李存審將兵討之。

translations.literal: Keyong sent Li Sizhao and Li Cunshen leading troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent Li Sizhao and Li Cunshen against him.

sentences.zh: 仁恭遣將以兵五萬救敬暉，嗣昭退保樂安，敬暉舉眾棄城而去。

translations.literal: Rengong sent a general with fifty thousand troops to rescue Jinghui; Sizhao withdrew to hold Le'an, and Jinghui raised his host, abandoned the city, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong sent fifty thousand men to rescue him; Li Sizhao fell back to Le'an, and Wang Jinghui abandoned the city with his troops.

sentences.zh: 先是，振武將契苾讓逐戍將石善友，據城叛。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Zhenwu officer Qibi Rang drove out the garrison commander Shi Shanyou, seized the city, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhenwu officer Qibi Rang had expelled garrison commander Shi Shanyou and seized the city in revolt.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭等進攻之，讓自燔死。

translations.literal: Sizhao and the others advanced to attack; Rang burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao attacked; Qibi Rang burned himself alive.

sentences.zh: 復取振武城，殺吐谷渾叛者二千餘人。

translations.literal: They recovered Zhenwu city and killed more than two thousand Tuyuhun rebels.
translations.idiomatic: They retook Zhenwu and executed more than two thousand Tuyuhun rebels.

sentences.zh: 克用怒嗣昭、存審失王敬暉，皆杖之，削其官。

translations.literal: Keyong was angry that Sizhao and Cunshen had lost Wang Jinghui; he caned them both and stripped their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong was furious that they had let Wang Jinghui escape; he flogged both men and stripped their ranks.

sentences.zh: 成汭行未至鄂州，馬殷遣大將許德勳將舟師萬餘人，雷彥威遣其將歐陽思將舟師三千餘人會於荊江口，乘虛襲江陵，庚戌，陷之，盡掠其人及貨財而去。

translations.literal: Cheng Ru's expedition had not yet reached Ezhou when Ma Yin sent the great general Xu Dexun with more than ten thousand naval troops, and Lei Yanwei sent his general Ouyang Si with more than three thousand naval troops to meet at Jingjiang mouth; seizing the void they raided Jiangling; on gengxu they took it, plundering all its people and goods before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Before Cheng Ru reached Ezhou, Ma Yin sent Xu Dexun with more than ten thousand sailors and Lei Yanwei sent Ouyang Si with three thousand more to rendezvous at Jingjiang. They struck the undefended Jiangling; on gengxu they took the city, looted its people and wealth, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 將士亡其家，皆無鬥志。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers had lost their homes and all lacked fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ru's men had lost their homes and had no will to fight.

sentences.zh: 李神福聞其將至，自乘輕舟前覘之，謂諸將曰：「彼戰艦雖多而不相屬，易制也，當急擊之！」

translations.literal: Li Shenfu heard they were coming, himself took a light boat forward to reconnoiter, and told the generals: "Their warships are many but not linked together—easy to control; we should strike them urgently!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing they were coming, Li Shenfu took a light boat forward to scout and told his commanders, "Their fleet is huge but scattered—they are easy to handle. Strike at once!"

sentences.zh: 壬子，神福遣其將秦裴、楊戎將眾數千逆擊汭於君山，大破之，因風縱火，焚其艦，士卒皆潰，汭赴水死，獲其戰艦二百艘。

translations.literal: On renzi, Shenfu sent his generals Qin Pei and Yang Rong with several thousand men to meet Ru in counterattack at Jun Mountain, routing him utterly; riding the wind they set fires and burned his ships; officers and soldiers all fled; Ru threw himself into the water and died; two hundred of his warships were captured.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Li Shenfu sent Qin Pei and Yang Rong with several thousand men to intercept Cheng Ru at Jun Mountain. They routed his fleet, set it ablaze in a favorable wind, and drove his troops into the water. Cheng Ru drowned; two hundred warships were captured.

sentences.zh: 韓勍聞之，亦引兵去。

translations.literal: Han Qin heard of it and also withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qin heard the news, he withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 許德勳還過岳州，刺史鄧進忠開門具牛酒犒軍，德勳諭以禍福，進忠遂舉族遷於長沙。

translations.literal: Xu Dexun returned, passing Yuezhou; the prefect Deng Jinzhong opened the gates and prepared oxen and wine to reward the army; Dexun instructed him on fortune and misfortune, and Jinzhong thereupon moved his whole clan to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Xu Dexun passed Yuezhou. Prefect Deng Jinzhong opened the gates with oxen and wine to feast the army. Xu Dexun explained the stakes, and Deng moved his entire clan to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 馬殷以德勳為岳州刺史，以進忠為衡州刺史。

translations.literal: Ma Yin made Dexun prefect of Yuezhou and Jinzhong prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin made Xu Dexun prefect of Yuezhou and Deng Jinzhong prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 雷彥威狡獪殘忍，有父風，常泛舟焚掠鄰境，荊、鄂之間，殆至無人。

translations.literal: Lei Yanwei was cunning, cruel, and had his father's ways; he often sailed about burning and plundering neighboring territories, so that between Jing and E there were almost no people left.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Yanwei was as cunning and brutal as his father, raiding neighboring lands by boat until the country between Jing and E was nearly depopulated.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞畏朱全忠，自以官為尚書令，在全忠上，累表乞解去。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen feared Zhu Quanzhong; considering that his office as Director of the Imperial Secretariat ranked above Quanzhong's, he repeatedly memorialized begging to resign it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen feared Zhu Quanzhong. As Director of the Imperial Secretariat he outranked Zhu and repeatedly asked to resign the post.

sentences.zh: 詔復以茂貞為中書令。

translations.literal: An edict restored Maozhen as Chief Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The court restored Li Maozhen as Chief Councilor instead.

sentences.zh: 崔胤奏：「左右龍武、羽林、神策等軍名存實亡，侍衛單寡；

translations.literal: Cui Yin memorialized: "The Left and Right Dragon Martial, Feathered Forest, Divine Strategy, and other armies exist in name but are gone in substance; palace guard is thin and few;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin memorialized, "The Dragon Martial, Feathered Forest, and Divine Strategy armies exist in name only; the palace guard is dangerously thin;

sentences.zh: 請每軍募步兵四將，每將二百五十人，騎兵一將百人，合六千六百人，選其壯健者，分番侍衛，」從之。

translations.literal: I request that each army recruit four infantry commanders with two hundred fifty men each per commander, and one cavalry commander with one hundred men—in all six thousand six hundred men—and select the sturdiest to serve the guard in rotating shifts," and this was approved."
translations.idiomatic: recruit four infantry commanders of two hundred fifty men each and one cavalry commander of one hundred per army—six thousand six hundred in all—and rotate the strongest for palace duty." The emperor agreed."

sentences.zh: 令六軍諸衛副使、京兆尹鄭元規立格召募於市。

translations.literal: The deputy commissioners of the Six Armies guards and the Jingzhao magistrate Zheng Yuangui were ordered to set standards and recruit in the markets.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commissioners of the Six Armies and Jingzhao magistrate Zheng Yuangui were ordered to recruit in the markets by set standards.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠表穎州刺史朱友恭為武寧李度使。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong memorialized that Yingzhou prefect Zhu Yougong be made military commissioner of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong recommended Yingzhou prefect Zhu Yougong as military commissioner of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 朱友寧攻博昌，月餘不拔。

translations.literal: Zhu Youning attacked Bochang but for more than a month could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youning besieged Bochang for more than a month without success.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠怒，遣客將李捍往督之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was angry and sent the guest general Li Han to supervise the operation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong was furious and sent Li Han to hurry the siege.

sentences.zh: 捍至，友寧驅民丁十餘萬，負木石，牽牛驢，詣城南築土山，既成，並人畜木石排而築之，冤號聲聞數十里。

translations.literal: When Han arrived, Youning drove more than one hundred thousand civilian laborers, bearing timber and stone, leading oxen and donkeys, to the south of the city to build an earthen mound; when it was finished, men, livestock, timber, and stone were lined up and piled to build it; cries of injustice were heard for tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han arrived and Zhu Youning pressed more than a hundred thousand laborers, with timber, stone, oxen, and donkeys, to build a siege mound south of the city. Men and beasts were driven into the work in ranks; their wailing carried for miles.

sentences.zh: 俄而城陷，盡屠之。

translations.literal: Shortly the city fell and all were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell and every soul was put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 進拔臨淄，抵青州城下，遣別將攻登、萊。

translations.literal: He advanced to take Linzi, reached below Qingzhou city, and dispatched separate generals to attack Deng and Lai.
translations.idiomatic: He took Linzi, advanced to Qingzhou, and sent detachments against Deng and Lai.

sentences.zh: 淮南將王茂章會王師範弟萊州刺史師誨攻密州，拔之，斬其刺史劉康乂，以淮海都游奕使張訓為刺史。

translations.literal: The Huainan general Wang Maozhang joined Wang Shifan's younger brother, Laizhou prefect Shi Hui, to attack Mizhou, took it, beheaded its prefect Liu Kangyi, and made the Huaihai circuit roving inspector Zhang Xun prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan general Wang Maozhang joined Shifan's brother Shi Hui, prefect of Lai, attacked Mizhou, killed prefect Liu Kangyi, and installed Huaihai roving inspector Zhang Xun as the new prefect.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙亥，汴兵拔登州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on yihai, the Bianzhou troops took Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yihai, Bian troops captured Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 師範帥登、萊兵拒朱友寧於石樓，為兩柵。

translations.literal: Shifan led Deng and Lai troops to resist Zhu Youning at Shilou, forming two stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan led Deng and Lai troops to hold Zhu Youning at Shilou behind two stockades.

sentences.zh: 丙子，夜，友寧擊登州柵，柵中告急，師範趣茂章出戰，茂章案兵不動。

translations.literal: On bingzi, at night, Youning attacked the Dengzhou stockade; inside the stockade they reported urgency; Shifan urged Maozhang to go out and fight, but Maozhang held his troops and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: That night on bingzi Zhu Youning struck the Deng stockade. Shifan begged Wang Maozhang to sortie, but Maozhang held his men still.

sentences.zh: 友寧破登州柵，進攻萊州柵。

translations.literal: Youning broke the Dengzhou stockade and advanced to attack the Laizhou stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Youning broke the Deng stockade and turned on the Lai stockade.

sentences.zh: 比明，茂章度其兵力已疲，乃與師範合兵出戰，大破之。

translations.literal: By dawn Maozhang judged their forces already weary, then joined Shifan in combined sortie and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, judging the enemy spent, Maozhang joined Shifan and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 友寧旁自峻阜馳騎赴敵，馬僕，青州將張士梟斬之，傳首淮南。

translations.literal: Youning himself galloped from a steep height to join the fight; his horse fell; the Qingzhou general Zhang Shixiao beheaded him and sent the head to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Youning himself galloped down a ridge to the fight; his horse threw him and Qingzhou officer Zhang Shixiao took his head and sent it to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 兩鎮兵逐北至米河，俘斬萬計，魏博之兵殆盡。

translations.literal: The troops of the two circuits pursued north to Mi River; captives and slain numbered in the tens of thousands; Weibo's army was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies pursued to Mi River, killing and capturing tens of thousands; Weibo's force was nearly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 全忠聞友寧死，自將兵二十萬晝夜兼行赴之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong heard Youning was dead and personally led two hundred thousand troops, traveling day and night without rest, to hurry there.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Youning's death, Zhu Quanzhong marched two hundred thousand men day and night to the scene.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬子，至臨朐，命諸將攻青州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renzi, he reached Linqu and ordered the generals to attack Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renzi, he reached Linqu and ordered an assault on Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王師範出戰，汴兵大破之。

translations.literal: Wang Shifan came out to fight; the Bianzhou troops routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan sortied and was crushed by the Bian army.

sentences.zh: 王茂章閉壘示怯，伺汴兵稍懈，毀柵而出，驅馳疾戰，戰酣退坐，召諸將飲酒，已而復戰。

translations.literal: Wang Maozhang closed his ramparts showing weakness, waited until the Bian troops slackened slightly, tore down the stockade and came out, driving in swift battle; when the fighting was fierce he withdrew to sit, summoned the generals to drink wine, then fought again.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maozhang shut his gates as if afraid, then when the Bian troops relaxed, broke out, fought furiously, withdrew to drink with his officers, and attacked again.

sentences.zh: 全忠登高望見之，問降者，知為茂章，歎曰：「使吾得此人為將，天下不足平也！」

translations.literal: Quanzhong climbed high and saw it; he asked surrendered men and learned it was Maozhang; he sighed and said: "If I could have this man as a general, the realm would not be hard to pacify!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong watched from a height, learned from prisoners it was Maozhang, and sighed, "With a general like that, pacifying the realm would be easy!"

sentences.zh: 至晡，汴兵乃退。

translations.literal: By the hour of shen the Bianzhou troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: By late afternoon the Bian army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 茂章度眾寡不敵，是夕，引軍還。

translations.literal: Maozhang judged that few could not match many; that evening he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he was outnumbered, Maozhang withdrew that night.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣曹州刺史楊師厚追之，及於輔唐。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Caozhou prefect Yang Shihou in pursuit and caught up at Futang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Caozhou prefect Yang Shihou in pursuit and overtook him at Futang.

sentences.zh: 茂章命先鋒指揮使李虔裕將五百騎為殿，虔裕殊死戰，師厚擒而殺之。

translations.literal: Maozhang ordered the vanguard commander Li Qianyu to lead five hundred cavalry as rearguard; Qianyu fought to the death; Shihou captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang left five hundred horsemen under Li Qianyu as rearguard; Li fought to the death and Yang Shihou killed him.

sentences.zh: 師厚，穎州人也。

translations.literal: Shihou was a man of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shihou was from Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 張訓聞茂章去，謂諸將曰：「汴人將至，何以御之？」

translations.literal: Zhang Xun heard Maozhang had left and said to the generals: "The Bian men are coming—how shall we resist them?"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Maozhang had gone, Zhang Xun asked his officers, "The Bian army is coming—how do we hold them?"

sentences.zh: 諸將請焚城大掠而歸。

translations.literal: The generals asked to burn the city, plunder greatly, and return.
translations.idiomatic: They urged burning the city, looting everything, and retreating.

sentences.zh: 訓曰：「不可。」

translations.literal: Xun said: "That cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun refused."

sentences.zh: 封府庫，植旗幟於城上，遣羸弱居前，自以精兵殿其後而去。

translations.literal: He sealed the treasury stores, planted banners on the city walls, sent the weak ahead and himself took crack troops as rearguard in departing.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the treasury, raised banners on the walls, sent the weak ahead with elite troops as rearguard, and marched out.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣左踏白指揮使王檀攻密州，既至，望旗幟，數日乃敢入城。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent the Left Tread-White commander Wang Tan to attack Mizhou; when he arrived he saw the banners and only after several days dared enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Wang Tan against Mizhou; seeing the banners, he waited several days before entering.

sentences.zh: 見府庫城邑皆完，遂不復追。

translations.literal: Seeing the treasury stores and city intact, he did not pursue further.
translations.idiomatic: Finding treasury and city intact, he did not pursue.

sentences.zh: 訓全軍而還。

translations.literal: Xun returned with the whole army intact.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun brought his whole force home safely.

sentences.zh: 全忠以檀為密州刺史。

translations.literal: Quanzhong made Tan prefect of Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong made Wang Tan prefect of Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以山南西道留後王宗賀為節度使。

translations.literal: On dingmao, the Shanannan West Circuit acting military commissioner Wang Zonghe was made full military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Wang Zonghe, acting commissioner of Shanannan West, was confirmed as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 睦州刺史陳詢叛錢鏐，舉兵攻蘭溪，鏐遣指揮使方永珍擊之。

translations.literal: Muzhou prefect Chen Xun rebelled against Qian Liu, raised troops to attack Lanxi, and Liu sent the commander Fang Yongzhen to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhou prefect Chen Xun rebelled against Qian Liu and attacked Lanxi; Liu sent Fang Yongzhen against him.

sentences.zh: 武安都指揮使杜建徽與詢連姻，鏐疑之，建徽不言。

translations.literal: The Wu'an overall commander Du Jianhui was connected to Xun by marriage; Liu suspected him, but Jianhui said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu'an commander Du Jianhui was related to Chen Xun by marriage. Qian Liu suspected him, but Du said nothing.

sentences.zh: 會詢親吏來奔，得建徽與詢書，皆勸戒之辭，鏐乃悅。

translations.literal: It happened that Xun's intimate clerk came over in surrender; they obtained letters between Jianhui and Xun, all words of admonition and restraint, and Liu was then pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen's clerk defected with letters between Du and Chen—all urging restraint—Qian Liu was reassured.

sentences.zh: 建徽從兄建思譖建徽私蓄兵仗，謀作亂。

translations.literal: Jianhui's cousin Jiansi slandered Jianhui for privately storing arms and plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Du's cousin Du Jiansi accused him of hoarding weapons and plotting revolt.

sentences.zh: 鏐使人索之，建徽方食，使者直入臥內，建徽不顧，鏐以是益親重之。

translations.literal: Liu sent men to search for them; Jianhui was just eating; the envoys went straight into the bedchamber; Jianhui paid no heed; Liu for this reason esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent men to search his quarters while Du was at supper; they walked into his bedroom and Du ignored them. Liu trusted him all the more.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊辰朔，朱全忠留齊州刺史楊師厚攻青州，身歸大梁。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day of the wuchen new moon, Zhu Quanzhong left Qizhou prefect Yang Shihou to attack Qingzhou and himself returned to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuchen, the first day of the month, Zhu Quanzhong left Yang Shihou to besiege Qingzhou and returned to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，加西川節度使西平王王建守司徒，進爵蜀王。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Xichuan military commissioner Prince of Xiping Wang Jian was further appointed acting Minister of Education and advanced to Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Wang Jian of Xichuan, Prince of Xiping, was made acting Minister of Education and raised to Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 前渝州刺史王宗本言於王建，請出兵取荊南。

translations.literal: The former Yuzhou prefect Wang Zongben spoke to Wang Jian, asking to send troops to take Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Former Yuzhou prefect Wang Zongben urged Wang Jian to seize Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 建從之，以宗本為開道都指揮使，將兵下峽。

translations.literal: Jian agreed and made Zongben overall commander for opening the route, leading troops down the gorges.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian agreed, made him commander for opening the route, and sent him down the Yangtze gorges.

sentences.zh: 初，寧國節度使田頵破馮弘鐸，詣廣陵謝楊行密，因求池、歙為巡屬，行密不許。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Ningguo military commissioner Tian Jun had defeated Feng Hongduo, went to Guangling to thank Yang Xingmi, and thereby asked that Chi and She be made his patrol dependencies; Xingmi did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ningguo commissioner Tian Jun, after defeating Feng Hongduo, went to Guangling to thank Yang Xingmi and asked to add Chi and She to his command. Xingmi refused.

sentences.zh: 行密左右下及獄吏，皆救賂於頵，頵怒曰：「吏知吾將下獄邪！」

translations.literal: Xingmi's attendants and prison clerks all demanded bribes from Jun; Jun angrily said: "Do the clerks know I am about to go to prison!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi's attendants and jailers all demanded bribes from Tian Jun, who raged, "Do they think I'm headed for prison?"

sentences.zh: 及還，指廣陵南門曰：「吾不可復入此矣！」

translations.literal: On returning he pointed at Guangling's south gate and said: "I cannot enter here again!"
translations.idiomatic: On his return he pointed at Guangling's south gate and said, "I will never enter that city again!"

sentences.zh: 頵兵強財富，好攻取。

translations.literal: Jun's troops were strong and his wealth abundant; he loved attacking and seizing.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun was strong and wealthy and loved conquest.

sentences.zh: 行密既定淮南，欲保境息民，每抑止之，頵不從。

translations.literal: After Xingmi had settled Huainan, he wished to secure the borders and give the people rest, and always restrained him, but Jun would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: After securing Huainan, Yang Xingmi wanted peace on the borders and constantly held Tian Jun back, but Jun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及解釋錢鏐，頵尤恨之，陰有叛志。

translations.literal: When Qian Liu was released from confinement, Jun hated this all the more and secretly harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang made peace with Qian Liu, Tian Jun hated it all the more and secretly planned rebellion.

sentences.zh: 李神福言於行密曰：「頵必反，宜早圖之。」

translations.literal: Li Shenfu said to Xingmi: "Jun is certain to rebel; he should be plotted against early."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu told Yang Xingmi, "Tian Jun will rebel—you should move against him soon."

sentences.zh: 行密曰：「頵有大功，反狀未露，今殺之，諸將人人自危矣！」

translations.literal: Xingmi said: "Jun has great merit; signs of rebellion are not yet exposed; to kill him now would make every general feel himself in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi replied, "He has great merit and his treason is not yet plain. Kill him now and every general will panic."

sentences.zh: 頵有良將曰康儒，與頵謀議多不合，行密知之，擢儒為廬州刺史。

translations.literal: Jun had a fine general named Kang Ru whose counsel often did not agree with Jun's; Xingmi knew this and promoted Ru to prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun's able general Kang Ru often disagreed with him. Yang Xingmi knew this and made Kang prefect of Lu.

sentences.zh: 頵以儒為貳於己，族之。

translations.literal: Jun considered Ru disloyal to himself and executed his whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun took this as disloyalty and exterminated Kang Ru's clan.

sentences.zh: 儒曰：「吾死，田公亡無日矣！」

translations.literal: Ru said: "When I die, Lord Tian's destruction will not be long delayed!"
translations.idiomatic: Kang Ru said before he died, "When I die, Lord Tian will not last long!"

sentences.zh: 頵遂與潤州團練使安仁義同舉兵，仁義悉焚東塘戰艦。

translations.literal: Jun thereupon joined Runzhou training commissioner An Renyi in raising troops together; Renyi burned all the warships at East Dike.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun then rose with Runzhou commissioner An Renyi, who burned the warships at East Dike.

sentences.zh: 頵遣二使詐為商人，詣壽州約奉國節度使朱延壽，行密將尚公乃遇之，曰：「非商人也。」

translations.literal: Jun sent two envoys disguised as merchants to Shouzhou to arrange with the Fengguo military commissioner Zhu Yanshou; Xingmi's general Shang Gongnai met them and said: "These are not merchants."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun sent two envoys disguised as merchants to Shouzhou to win over Fengguo commissioner Zhu Yanshou. Yang's officer Shang Gongnai intercepted them and said, "These are not merchants."

sentences.zh: 殺一人，得其書，以告行密。

translations.literal: He killed one man, obtained their letter, and reported to Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: He killed one, seized their letters, and reported to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 行密召李神福於鄂州，神福恐杜洪邀之，宣言奉命攻荊南，勒兵具舟楫。

translations.literal: Xingmi summoned Li Shenfu from Ezhou; Shenfu feared Du Hong would intercept him, proclaimed he was ordered to attack Jingnan, and mustered troops and prepared boats.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi summoned Li Shenfu from Ezhou. Shenfu feared Du Hong might block him, announced he was ordered to attack Jingnan, and mobilized ships.

sentences.zh: 及暮，遂沿江東下，始告將士以討田頵。

translations.literal: At dusk he then went downstream along the river, and only then told the officers and soldiers they were to punish Tian Jun.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he sailed downriver and only then told his men they were marching against Tian Jun.

sentences.zh: 己丑，安仁義襲常州，常州刺史李遇逆戰，極口罵仁義，仁義曰：「彼敢辱我，必有備。」

translations.literal: On jichou, An Renyi raided Changzhou; Changzhou prefect Li Yu met him in battle and cursed Renyi with the utmost abuse; Renyi said: "He dares insult me—he must be prepared."
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, An Renyi attacked Changzhou. Prefect Li Yu met him in battle and cursed him foully. Renyi said, "He insults me so boldly—he must be ready."

sentences.zh: 乃引去。

translations.literal: He then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，行密以王茂章為潤州行營招討使，擊仁義，不克，使徐溫將兵會之。

translations.literal: On renchen, Xingmi made Wang Maozhang campaigning commissioner for Runzhou to attack Renyi; he could not overcome him and sent Xu Wen with troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Yang Xingmi made Wang Maozhang commander against Runzhou. Wang failed to break An Renyi, so Yang sent Xu Wen to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 溫易其衣服旗幟，皆如茂章兵，仁義不知益兵，復出戰，溫奮擊，破之。

translations.literal: Wen changed his men's clothing and banners to resemble Maozhang's troops; Renyi did not know reinforcements had been added and came out to fight again; Wen struck fiercely and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen dressed his men like Maozhang's troops. An Renyi, not knowing reinforcements had arrived, sortied again and was crushed.

sentences.zh: 行密夫人，朱延壽之姊也。

translations.literal: Xingmi's wife was Zhu Yanshou's elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi's wife was Zhu Yanshou's elder sister.

sentences.zh: 行密狎侮延壽，延壽怨怒，陰與田頵通謀。

translations.literal: Xingmi treated Yanshou familiarly and insulted him; Yanshou resented and raged and secretly communicated plans with Tian Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi treated Zhu Yanshou with casual insults; Zhu brooded and secretly plotted with Tian Jun.

sentences.zh: 頵遣前進士杜荀鶴至壽州，與延壽相結，又遣至大梁告朱全忠，全忠大喜，遣兵屯宿州以應之。

translations.literal: Jun sent the former jinshi Du Xunhe to Shouzhou to join with Yanshou, and also sent him to Daliang to inform Zhu Quanzhong; Quanzhong was greatly pleased and sent troops to camp at Suzhou in response.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun sent former jinshi Du Xunhe to Shouzhou to ally with Zhu Yanshou and then to Daliang to inform Zhu Quanzhong, who gladly stationed troops at Suzhou in support.

sentences.zh: 荀鶴，池州人也。

translations.literal: Xunhe was a man of Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xunhe was from Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 楊師厚屯臨朐，聲言將之密州，留輜重於臨朐。

translations.literal: Yang Shihou camped at Linqu, proclaiming he would go to Mizhou, and left baggage at Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shihou camped at Linqu, announced he was marching on Mizhou, and left his baggage there.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸卯，王師範出兵攻臨朐，師厚伏兵奮擊，大破之，殺萬餘人，獲師範弟師克。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guimao, Wang Shifan sent troops to attack Linqu; Shihou's ambush troops struck fiercely and routed them utterly, killing more than ten thousand men and capturing Shifan's younger brother Shike.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guimao, Wang Shifan attacked Linqu. Yang Shihou's ambush slaughtered more than ten thousand and captured Shifan's brother Shike.

sentences.zh: 明日，萊州兵五千救青州。

translations.literal: The next day five thousand Laizhou troops came to rescue Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day five thousand men from Lai marched to relieve Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 師厚邀擊之，殺獲殆盡，遂徙寨抵其城下。

translations.literal: Shihou intercepted and struck them, killing and capturing nearly all, then moved his camp to press against the city below.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shihou intercepted and nearly annihilated them, then moved his camp to the foot of the city walls.

sentences.zh: 朱延壽謀頗洩，楊行密詐為目疾，對延壽使者多錯亂所見，或觸柱仆地。

translations.literal: Zhu Yanshou's plot leaked rather openly; Yang Xingmi pretended eye disease, and toward Yanshou's envoys often confused what he saw or bumped pillars and fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yanshou's plot leaked. Yang Xingmi feigned blindness, confused his envoys, and sometimes stumbled into pillars.

sentences.zh: 謂夫人曰：「吾不幸失明，諸子皆幼，軍府事當悉以授三舅。」

translations.literal: He told his wife: "I have unfortunately gone blind; the sons are all young; military and government affairs should all be entrusted to Third Uncle."
translations.idiomatic: He told his wife, "I have gone blind, my sons are young, and all military affairs must go to your third brother."

sentences.zh: 夫人屢以書報延壽，行密又自遣召之，陰令徐溫為之備。

translations.literal: The wife repeatedly reported by letter to Yanshou; Xingmi also himself sent to summon him, while secretly ordering Xu Wen to prepare against him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife wrote repeatedly to Zhu Yanshou. Yang Xingmi summoned him openly while secretly ordering Xu Wen to prepare.

sentences.zh: 延壽至廣陵，行密迎及寢門，執而殺之。

translations.literal: Yanshou reached Guangling; Xingmi met him at the bedroom gate, seized him, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yanshou reached Guangling, Yang Xingmi met him at the bedroom door, seized him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 部兵驚擾，徐溫諭之，皆聽命，遂斬延壽兄弟，黜朱夫人。

translations.literal: His troops were alarmed and disturbed; Xu Wen instructed them and all obeyed; then Yanshou's brothers were beheaded and Lady Zhu was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: His troops panicked until Xu Wen calmed them. Yang then executed Zhu Yanshou's brothers and demoted Lady Zhu.

sentences.zh: 初，延壽赴召，其妻王氏謂曰：「君此行吉凶未可知，願日發一使以安我！」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yanshou answered the summons, his wife Lady Wang said: "On this journey fortune and misfortune are unknown; I wish you would send one envoy each day to reassure me!"
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhu left, his wife Lady Wang said, "This journey may end badly—send me a messenger every day."

sentences.zh: 一日，使不至，王氏曰：「事可知矣！」

translations.literal: One day no envoy came; Lady Wang said: "The matter can be known now!"
translations.idiomatic: When one day no messenger came, she said, "Now I know."

sentences.zh: 部分僮僕，授兵闔門，捕騎至，乃集家人，聚寶貨，發百燎焚府捨，曰：「妾誓不以皎然之軀為仇人所辱。」

translations.literal: She arrayed servants, distributed weapons, closed the gates; when arresting riders arrived she then gathered the family, collected treasures, lit a hundred fires to burn the mansion, and said: "This wife vows not to let her bright body be shamed by enemies."
translations.idiomatic: She armed the household, barred the gates, and when soldiers came gathered her family, heaped treasure, set the mansion ablaze with a hundred torches, and said, "I will not let my body be shamed by enemies."

sentences.zh: 赴火而死。

translations.literal: She threw herself into the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself into the flames.

sentences.zh: 延壽用法嚴，好以寡擊眾，嘗遣二百人與汴兵戰，有一人應留者，請行，延壽以違命，立斬之。

translations.literal: Yanshou applied the law strictly, loved to use the few to strike the many; he once sent two hundred men to fight Bianzhou troops; one man who should have stayed asked to go; Yanshou for disobeying orders beheaded him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yanshou was severe in discipline and loved fighting outnumbered. Once he sent two hundred men against Bian troops; one man who should have stayed behind asked to go and Zhu executed him instantly for disobedience.

sentences.zh: 田頵襲升州，得李神福妻子，善遇之。

translations.literal: Tian Jun raided Shengzhou, captured Li Shenfu's wife and children, and treated them well.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun seized Shengzhou and captured Li Shenfu's family, treating them kindly.

sentences.zh: 神福自鄂州東下，頵遣使謂之曰：「公見機，與公分地而王；

translations.literal: Shenfu came down the river east from Ezhou; Jun sent an envoy telling him: "Sir, read the moment—divide territory with me and be king;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu marched east from Ezhou. Tian Jun sent envoys saying, "Read the times, divide the land with me, and be a king;

sentences.zh: 不然，妻子無遺！」

translations.literal: otherwise your wife and children will not survive!"
translations.idiomatic: or your wife and children will not survive!"

sentences.zh: 神福曰：「吾以卒伍事吳王，今為上將，義不以妻子易其志。

translations.literal: Shenfu said: "I served the King of Wu as a common soldier; now I am a great general—by righteousness I will not trade my resolve for wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu replied, "I served the King of Wu as a common soldier and am now a great general. I will not trade my loyalty for my family.

sentences.zh: 頵有老母，不顧而反，三綱且不知，烏足與言乎！」

translations.literal: Jun has an old mother yet disobeys and rebels—he does not even know the Three Bonds; how is he fit to speak with!"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun has an aged mother yet rebels against his lord—he does not even understand the Three Bonds. He is not worth addressing!"

sentences.zh: 斬使者而進，士卒皆感勵。

translations.literal: He beheaded the envoy and advanced; officers and soldiers were all moved and inspired.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded the envoys and marched on; his soldiers were inspired.

sentences.zh: 頵遣其將王檀、汪建將水軍逆戰。

translations.literal: Jun sent his generals Wang Tan and Wang Jian to lead the naval forces in counterattack.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun sent Wang Tan and Wang Jian with the fleet to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 丁未，神福至吉陽磯，與壇、建遇。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Shenfu reached Jiyang Ford and met Tan and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Li Shenfu reached Jiyang Ford and met them.

sentences.zh: 壇、建執其子承鼎示之，神福命左右射之。

translations.literal: Tan and Jian held up his son Chengdong to show him; Shenfu ordered those at his side to shoot at him.
translations.idiomatic: They held up his son Chengdong. Li Shenfu ordered his men to shoot at the boy.

sentences.zh: 神福謂諸將曰：「彼眾我寡，當以奇取勝。」

translations.literal: Shenfu told the generals: "They are many and we are few—we must win by surprise."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu told his officers, "They outnumber us—we must win by stratagem."

sentences.zh: 及暮，合戰，神福陽敗，引舟溯流而上。

translations.literal: At dusk they joined battle; Shenfu pretended defeat and drew his boats upstream.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk they fought. Li Shenfu feigned defeat and sailed upstream.

sentences.zh: 壇、建追之，神福復還，順流擊之。

translations.literal: Tan and Jian pursued; Shenfu turned back and struck downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Tan and Jian pursued; Shenfu turned and attacked downstream.

sentences.zh: 壇、建樓船大列火炬，神福令軍中曰：「望火炬則擊之。」

translations.literal: Tan and Jian's tower ships arrayed torches in great numbers; Shenfu ordered the army: "When you see torches, strike them."
translations.idiomatic: Their tower ships lined up torches. Li Shenfu ordered, "Strike wherever you see fire."

sentences.zh: 壇、建軍皆滅火，旗幟交雜，神福因風縱火，焚其艦，壇、建大敗，士卒焚溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Tan and Jian's army all extinguished their fires; banners and flags became tangled; Shenfu rode the wind to set fires, burned their ships; Tan and Jian were utterly routed; officers and soldiers burned and drowned in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: They doused their lights in confusion. Li Shenfu set the fleet ablaze in a favorable wind. Tan and Jian were routed; countless men burned or drowned.

sentences.zh: 戊申，又戰於皖口，壇、建僅以身免。

translations.literal: On wushen they fought again at Wankou; Tan and Jian barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen they fought again at Wankou; Tan and Jian barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 獲徐綰，行密以檻車載之，遺錢鏐。

translations.literal: Xu Wan was captured; Xingmi sent him in a caged cart as a gift to Qian Liu.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Xu Wan. Yang Xingmi sent him in a cage to Qian Liu.

sentences.zh: 鏐剖其心以祭高渭。

translations.literal: Liu cut out his heart to sacrifice to Gao Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu cut out his heart to sacrifice to Gao Wei.

sentences.zh: 頵聞壇、建敗，自將水軍逆戰，神福曰：「賊棄城而來，此天亡也！」

translations.literal: Jun heard Tan and Jian were defeated and personally led the navy to meet in battle; Shenfu said: "The rebels abandon their city to come—this is Heaven's destruction of them!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the defeat, Tian Jun led his fleet in person. Li Shenfu said, "They left their city to fight—Heaven is destroying them!"

sentences.zh: 臨江堅壁不戰，遣行告行密，請發步兵斷其歸路。

translations.literal: He held firm walls along the river and would not fight, sent a courier to tell Xingmi, and asked that infantry be sent to cut off their return route.
translations.idiomatic: He held the river line without fighting and asked Yang Xingmi to send infantry to cut off Tian Jun's retreat.

sentences.zh: 行密遣漣水制置使台濛將兵應之。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent the Lianshui commissioner Tai Meng with troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent Lianshui commissioner Tai Meng to support him.

sentences.zh: 王茂章攻潤州，久未下，行密命茂章引兵會濛擊頵。

translations.literal: Wang Maozhang attacked Runzhou but for a long time could not take it; Xingmi ordered Maozhang to lead troops to join Meng in striking Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maozhang had long failed to take Runzhou; Yang Xingmi ordered him to join Tai Meng against Tian Jun.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，汴將劉重霸拔棣州，執刺史邵播，殺之。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the Bianzhou general Liu Zhongba took Dizhou, seized the prefect Shao Bo, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Bian general Liu Zhongba took Dizhou, seized prefect Shao Bo, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，朱全忠如洛陽，遇疾，復還大梁。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Zhu Quanzhong went to Luoyang, fell ill, and returned again to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Zhu Quanzhong went to Luoyang, fell ill, and returned to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 戊午，王師範遣副使李嗣業及弟師悅請降於楊師厚，曰：「師範非敢背德，韓全誨、李茂貞以朱書御札使之舉兵，師範不敢違。」

translations.literal: On wuwu, Wang Shifan sent his deputy envoy Li Siye and younger brother Shi Yue to beg surrender from Yang Shihou, saying: "Shifan does not dare turn against virtue; Han Quanhui and Li Maozhen used vermilion imperial rescripts to make him raise troops—Shifan dared not disobey."
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Wang Shifan sent Li Siye and his brother Shi Yue to surrender to Yang Shihou, saying, "I did not rebel willingly—Han Quanhui and Li Maozhen used imperial rescripts in vermilion to force me to arms."

sentences.zh: 仍請以其弟師魯為質。

translations.literal: He also asked to offer his younger brother Shilu as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: He offered his brother Shilu as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 時朱全忠聞李茂貞、楊崇本將起兵逼京畿，恐其復劫天子西去，欲迎車駕都洛陽，乃受師範降，選諸將使守登、萊、淄、棣等州，即以師範權淄青留後。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Quanzhong heard Li Maozhen and Yang Chongben would raise troops to press the capital region; he feared they would again seize the Son of Heaven and go west; he wished to welcome the imperial carriage to make Luoyang the capital; he then accepted Shifan's surrender, chose generals to guard Deng, Lai, Zi, Di, and other prefectures, and made Shifan acting Ziqing military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong heard Li Maozhen and Yang Chongben were marching on the capital and feared another abduction of the emperor westward. He planned to move the court to Luoyang, accepted Shifan's surrender, garrisoned Deng, Lai, Zi, and Di, and made him acting Ziqing commissioner.

sentences.zh: 師範仍言先遣行軍司馬劉鄩將兵五千據兗州，非其自專，願釋其罪。

translations.literal: Shifan still said he had earlier sent the campaigning marshal Liu Yun with five thousand troops to hold Yanzhou—not on his own authority—and wished his crime released.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan explained he had earlier sent Liu Yun with five thousand men to hold Yanzhou without acting on his own and asked clemency for him.

sentences.zh: 亦遣使語鄩。

translations.literal: He also sent an envoy to speak with Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent word to Liu Yun.

sentences.zh: 田頵聞台濛將至，自將步騎逆戰，留其將郭行頵以精兵二萬及王壇、汪建水軍屯蕪湖，以拒李神福。

translations.literal: Tian Jun heard Tai Meng was coming and personally led infantry and cavalry to meet in battle; he left his general Guo Xingjun with twenty thousand crack troops plus Wang Tan and Wang Jian's naval forces camped at Wuhu to resist Li Shenfu.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun heard Tai Meng was coming and marched out in person, leaving Guo Xingjun with twenty thousand elite troops and Wang Tan and Wang Jian's fleet at Wuhu to block Li Shenfu.

sentences.zh: 覘者言：「濛營寨褊小，才容二千人。」

translations.literal: Scouts said: "Meng's camp is narrow and small—it can hold only two thousand men."
translations.idiomatic: Scouts reported, "Meng's camp is tiny—barely two thousand men."

sentences.zh: 頵易之，不召外兵。

translations.literal: Jun took them lightly and did not summon outside troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun underestimated him and did not call up reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 濛入頵境，番陳而進，軍中笑其怯，濛曰：「頵宿將多謀，不可不備。」

translations.literal: Meng entered Jun's territory, advancing in rotating formations; the army laughed at his timidity; Meng said: "Jun is an old commander full of stratagems—we cannot fail to prepare."
translations.idiomatic: Tai Meng entered Tian Jun's territory in rotating columns. His men mocked his caution, but he said, "Tian Jun is a veteran full of tricks—we must be ready."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，戊辰，與頵遇於廣德。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on wuchen, he met Jun at Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on wuchen, they met at Guangde.

sentences.zh: 濛先以楊行密書遍賜頵將，皆下馬拜受。

translations.literal: Meng first distributed Yang Xingmi's letters widely to Jun's generals; all dismounted to bow and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Meng first distributed Yang Xingmi's letters to Tian Jun's officers, who all dismounted to receive them.

sentences.zh: 濛因其挫伏，縱兵擊之，頵兵遂敗。

translations.literal: Meng took advantage of their shaken morale, loosed troops to strike them, and Jun's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: While their morale was shaken, Tai Meng attacked and routed Tian Jun's army.

sentences.zh: 又戰於黃池，兵交，濛偽走，頵追之，遇伏，大敗，奔還宣州城守，濛引兵圍之。

translations.literal: They fought again at Huangchi; as troops clashed Meng feigned flight; Jun pursued and met an ambush, was utterly routed, fled back to hold Xuancheng, and Meng led troops to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangchi they clashed again. Tai Meng feigned retreat, lured Tian Jun into an ambush, and drove him back to Xuancheng, which Tai Meng besieged.

sentences.zh: 頵亟召蕪湖兵還，不得入。

translations.literal: Jun urgently summoned the Wuhu troops back but they could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun urgently recalled the Wuhu force, but it could not get in.

sentences.zh: 郭行悰、王壇、汪建及當塗、廣德諸戍皆帥其眾降。

translations.literal: Guo Xingcong, Wang Tan, Wang Jian, and the garrisons of Dangtu, Guangde, and others all led their hosts in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xingcong, Wang Tan, Wang Jian, and the garrisons of Dangtu and Guangde all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 行密以台濛已破田悰，命王茂章復引兵攻潤州。

translations.literal: Xingmi, since Tai Meng had already broken Tian Cong, ordered Wang Maozhang again to lead troops to attack Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Tian Jun broken, Yang Xingmi ordered Wang Maozhang to resume the attack on Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，夔州刺史侯矩從成汭救鄂州，汭死，矩奔還。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qizhou prefect Hou Ju had followed Cheng Ru to rescue Ezhou; when Ru died, Ju fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qizhou prefect Hou Ju had followed Cheng Ru to relieve Ezhou. When Ru died, Hou fled home.

sentences.zh: 會王宗本兵至，甲戌，矩以州降之，宗本遂定夔、忠、萬、施四州。

translations.literal: When Wang Zongben's troops arrived, on jiaxu, Ju surrendered the prefecture to him; Zongben then settled the four prefectures of Qi, Zhong, Wan, and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zongben arrived, on jiaxu Hou Ju surrendered Qizhou, and Zongben secured Qi, Zhong, Wan, and Shi.

sentences.zh: 王建復以矩為夔州刺史，更其姓名曰王宗矩。

translations.literal: Wang Jian again made Ju prefect of Qizhou and changed his name to Wang Zongju.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian reappointed him prefect of Qizhou and renamed him Wang Zongju.

sentences.zh: 宗矩，易州人也。

translations.literal: Zongju was a man of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongju was from Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀之議者，以瞿唐，蜀之險要，乃棄歸、峽，屯軍夔州。

translations.literal: Shu's advisers held that Qutang was Shu's strategic choke point, yet they abandoned Gui and Xia and stationed troops at Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's advisers said Qutang was the strategic pass, yet they abandoned Gui and Xia and garrisoned Qizhou instead.

sentences.zh: 建以宗本為武泰留後。

translations.literal: Jian made Zongben acting Wutai military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian made Wang Zongben acting commissioner of Wutai.

sentences.zh: 武泰軍舊治黔州，宗本以其地多瘴癘，清徙治涪州，建許之。

translations.literal: The Wutai army had formerly governed Qianzhou; Zongben because the region had much miasma requested to move the seat to Fuzhou, and Jian permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wutai had been based at Qianzhou, but Zongben asked to move to Fuzhou because of malaria; Wang Jian agreed.

sentences.zh: 葛從周急攻兗州，劉鄩使從周母乘板輿登城，謂從周曰：「劉將軍事我不異於汝，新婦輩皆安居，人各為其主，汝可察之。」

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou pressed the attack on Yanzhou; Liu Yun had Congzhou's mother ride a plank litter up the wall and told Congzhou: "General Liu treats me no differently from you; the new wives all live in peace—each man serves his lord; you may observe this."
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou pressed Yanzhou hard. Liu Yun had Ge's mother carried up the wall in a litter and told him, "General Liu treats me like family. Your wives are safe. Each man serves his lord—think on that."

sentences.zh: 從周歔欷而退，攻城為之緩。

translations.literal: Congzhou sighed and wept and withdrew; the siege was slowed for this.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou withdrew in tears and eased the assault.

sentences.zh: 鄩悉簡婦人及民之老疾不足當敵者出之，獨與少壯者同辛苦，分衣食，堅守以扞敵。

translations.literal: Yun sent out all women and civilians who were old, ill, or unfit to face the enemy; he alone shared hardship with the young and strong, divided food and clothing, and held firm to resist the foe.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun expelled women and civilians too old or weak to fight, shared hardship and rations with the young men, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 號令整肅，兵不為暴，民皆安堵，久之，外援既絕，節度副使王彥溫逾城出降，城上卒多從之，不可遏。

translations.literal: Orders were strict and orderly; troops did not act violently; the people all lived in peace; after a long time outside relief was cut off; the deputy military commissioner Wang Yanwen climbed over the wall to surrender; many soldiers on the wall followed and it could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline was strict and the people were unmolested. When relief failed, deputy commissioner Wang Yanwen climbed out to surrender and many soldiers followed unstoppably.

sentences.zh: 鄩遣人從容語彥溫曰：「軍士非素遣者，勿多與之俱。」

translations.literal: Yun sent someone calmly to tell Yanwen: "Soldiers not originally assigned—do not take too many with you."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun calmly told Yanwen, "Do not take too many men who were not originally under you."

sentences.zh: 又遣人徇於城上曰：「軍士非素遣從副使而敢擅往者，族之！」

translations.literal: He also sent someone to proclaim on the wall: "Any soldier not originally assigned to follow the deputy commissioner who dares go on his own—his clan will be exterminated!"
translations.idiomatic: He also proclaimed on the wall, "Any soldier who follows the deputy commissioner without original orders will have his clan exterminated!"

sentences.zh: 士卒皆惶惑不敢出。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were all fearful and confused and dared not go out.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were too afraid to leave.

sentences.zh: 敵人果疑彥溫，斬之城下，由是眾心益固。

translations.literal: The enemy indeed suspected Yanwen and beheaded him below the wall; thereby the people's hearts grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy suspected Yanwen and beheaded him below the wall, which only stiffened morale.

sentences.zh: 及王師範力屈，從周以禍福諭之，鄩曰：「受王公命守此城，一旦見王公失勢，不俟其命而降，非所以事上也。」

translations.literal: When Wang Shifan's strength was exhausted, Congzhou used fortune and misfortune to instruct him; Yun said: "I received Lord Wang's order to guard this city; to see Lord Wang lose power and surrender without awaiting his command is not how one serves a superior."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shifan was broken, Ge Congzhou urged surrender. Liu Yun said, "I was ordered to hold this city. I cannot surrender before my lord commands it—that is not loyalty."

sentences.zh: 及師範使者至，丁丑，始出降。

translations.literal: When Shifan's envoy arrived, on dingchou, he finally came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shifan's envoy arrived on dingchou, he finally surrendered.

sentences.zh: 從周為具繼裝，送鄩詣大梁。

translations.literal: Congzhou provided traveling gear and sent Yun to Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou equipped him for travel and sent him to Daliang.

sentences.zh: 鄩曰：「降將未受梁王寬釋之命，安敢乘馬衣裘乎！」

translations.literal: Yun said: "A surrendered general who has not yet received Prince of Liang's gracious pardon—how dare he ride a horse and wear furs!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun said, "A surrendered general who has not yet received the Prince of Liang's pardon—how dare I ride a horse or wear furs!"

sentences.zh: 乃素服乘驢至大梁。

translations.literal: He then went to Daliang in plain white dress riding a donkey.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Daliang in plain clothes on a donkey.

sentences.zh: 全忠賜之冠帶，辭；

translations.literal: Quanzhong bestowed cap and belt; he declined;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong offered him cap and belt; he refused;

sentences.zh: 請囚服入見，不許。

translations.literal: he asked to enter in prisoner's garb and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: asked to enter in prisoner's garb and was refused.
