sentences.zh: 全忠慰勞，飲之酒，辭以量小。

translations.literal: Quanzhong consoled and comforted him and offered wine; he declined on grounds of small capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong comforted him and offered wine; he declined, saying he could not drink much.

sentences.zh: 全忠曰：「取兗州，量何大邪！」

translations.literal: Quanzhong said: "When you took Yanzhou, how great was your capacity then!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong said, "When you held Yanzhou, your capacity was greater!"

sentences.zh: 以為元從都押牙。

translations.literal: He was made overall guard commander of the original followers.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief guard commander of Zhu's original followers.

sentences.zh: 是時四鎮將吏皆功臣、舊人，鄩一旦以降將居其上，諸將具軍禮拜於廷，鄩坐受自如，全忠益奇之。

translations.literal: At that time the generals and officials of the four circuits were all meritorious subjects and old companions; Yun suddenly as a surrendered general sat above them; the generals all performed military rites bowing in the hall; Yun sat receiving them as if natural; Quanzhong admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The four circuits' officers were all Zhu's old companions. Liu Yun, a surrendered general, sat above them and accepted their military salutes as if it were natural. Zhu Quanzhong admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 未幾，表為保大留後。

translations.literal: Before long he was memorialized as acting Baoda military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recommended as acting commissioner of Baoda.

sentences.zh: 葛從周久病，全忠以康懷英為泰寧節度使代之。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou had long been ill; Quanzhong made Kang Huaiying military commissioner of Taining to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou had been ill for a long time; Zhu Quanzhong replaced him with Kang Huaiying as Taining commissioner.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，宿衛都指揮使朱友倫與客擊球於左軍，墜馬而卒。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the palace guard overall commander Zhu Youlun played ball with guests in the Left Army, fell from his horse, and died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, palace guard commander Zhu Youlun was playing ball in the Left Army when he fell from his horse and died.

sentences.zh: 全忠悲怒，疑崔胤故為之，凡與同戲者十餘人盡殺之，遣其兄子友諒代典宿衛。

translations.literal: Quanzhong grieved and raged, suspected Cui Yin had done it on purpose, killed all more than ten who had played together, and sent his elder brother's son Youliang to take charge of the palace guard in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong grieved and raged, suspected Cui Yin of causing it, killed more than ten men who had played with him, and put his nephew Youliang in charge of the guard.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使趙匡凝遣兵襲荊南，朗人棄城走，匡凝表其弟匡明為荊南留後。

translations.literal: The Shannan East Circuit military commissioner Zhao Kuangning sent troops to raid Jingnan; the Langzhou men abandoned the city and fled; Kuangning memorialized his younger brother Kuangming as acting Jingnan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan East commissioner Zhao Kuangning raided Jingnan; the defenders fled; he made his brother Kuangming acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時天子微弱，諸道財賦多不上供，惟匡凝兄弟委輸不絕。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was weak; the various circuits' taxes and levies mostly were not forwarded; only the Kuangning brothers' deliveries never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was weak and most circuits stopped paying tribute, but the Kuangning brothers kept sending revenue without fail.

sentences.zh: 楊行密求兵於錢鏐，鏐遣方永珍屯潤州，從弟鎰屯宣州。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi begged troops from Qian Liu; Liu sent Fang Yongzhen to camp at Runzhou and his younger cousin Yi to camp at Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi asked Qian Liu for troops; Liu sent Fang Yongzhen to Runzhou and his cousin Yi to Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 又遣指揮使楊習攻睦州。

translations.literal: He also sent the commander Yang Xi to attack Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Yang Xi against Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔、邠州屢出兵近京畿，朱全忠疑其復有劫遷之謀，十一月，發騎兵屯河中。

translations.literal: Fengxiang and Binzhou repeatedly sent troops near the capital region; Zhu Quanzhong suspected they again plotted to seize and move the emperor; in the eleventh month he sent cavalry to camp at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang and Binzhou repeatedly sent troops near the capital. Zhu Quanzhong feared another abduction of the emperor and in the eleventh month stationed cavalry at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙亥，田頵帥死士數百出戰，台濛陽退以示弱。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yihai, Tian Jun led several hundred death-defying warriors out to fight; Tai Meng pretended retreat to show weakness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yihai, Tian Jun led several hundred picked men out to fight; Tai Meng feigned retreat.

sentences.zh: 頵兵逾濠而鬥，濛急擊之。

translations.literal: Jun's troops crossed the moat to fight; Meng struck them urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun's men crossed the moat; Tai Meng struck hard.

sentences.zh: 頵不勝，還走城，橋陷墜馬，斬之，其眾猶戰，以頵首示之，乃潰，濛遂克宣州。

translations.literal: Jun could not overcome them, fled back toward the city; the bridge collapsed and he fell from his horse and was beheaded; his host still fought; when Jun's head was shown them they then fled; Meng thereupon took Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun was beaten back; the bridge collapsed under him and he was beheaded. His men fought on until his head was shown, then they broke. Tai Meng took Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 初，行密與頵閭裡，少相善，約為兄弟，及頵首至廣陵，行密視之泣下，赦其母殷氏，行密與諸子皆以子孫禮事之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xingmi and Jun were from the same village, friendly in youth, and had covenanted as brothers; when Jun's head reached Guangling, Xingmi looked at it and wept; he pardoned Jun's mother Lady Yin; Xingmi and his sons all served her with grandchildren's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi and Tian Jun had been village friends and sworn brothers. When Tian's head reached Guangling, Yang wept, pardoned his mother Lady Yin, and he and his sons treated her with a grandson's respect.

sentences.zh: 行密以李神福為寧國節度使，神福以杜洪未平，固讓不拜。

translations.literal: Xingmi made Li Shenfu military commissioner of Ningguo; Shenfu because Du Hong was not yet pacified firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi made Li Shenfu commissioner of Ningguo, but Shenfu refused while Du Hong was still unconquered.

sentences.zh: 宣州長史合肥駱知祥善治金谷，觀察牙推沈文昌為文精敏，嘗為頵草檄罵行密，行密以知祥為淮南支計官，文昌為節度分推。

translations.literal: Xuancheng chief administrator Luo Zhixiang of Hefei was skilled at managing finances; the surveillance office aide Shen Wenchang was refined and quick in writing and had once drafted Jun's proclamation cursing Xingmi; Xingmi made Zhixiang Huainan branch accounting officer and Wenchang circuit branch aide.
translations.idiomatic: Xuancheng chief administrator Luo Zhixiang of Hefei was skilled at finance; aide Shen Wenchang, who had drafted Tian Jun's denunciations of Yang Xingmi, was made branch accountant and circuit aide respectively.

sentences.zh: 文昌湖州人也。

translations.literal: Wenchang was a man of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenchang was from Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，頵每戰不勝，輒欲殺錢傳瓘，其母及宣州都虞候郭師從常保護之。

translations.literal: Earlier, whenever Jun was defeated in battle he would want to kill Qian Chuanjian; his mother and the Xuancheng overall commander Guo Shicong constantly protected him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tian Jun lost a battle he wanted to kill Qian Chuanjian; his mother and Xuancheng commander Guo Shicong always protected him.

sentences.zh: 師從，合肥人，頵之婦弟也。

translations.literal: Shicong was a man of Hefei, Jun's wife's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shicong of Hefei was Tian Jun's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 頵敗，傳瓘歸杭州，錢鏐以師從為鎮東都虞候。

translations.literal: When Jun was defeated, Chuanjian returned to Hangzhou; Qian Liu made Shicong Zhendong overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Tian Jun's defeat, Chuanjian returned to Hangzhou and Qian Liu made Guo Shicong overall commander of Zhendong.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以禮部尚書獨孤損為兵部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Minister of Rites Dugu Sun was made Vice Minister of War and Associate Chief Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Dugu Sun, Minister of Rites, was made Vice Minister of War and Associate Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 損，及之從曾孫也。

translations.literal: Sun was a great-great-grandson of Dugu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Sun was a great-great-grandson of Dugu Ji.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎兼戶部尚書、同平章事裴贄罷為左僕射。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Minister of Revenue and Associate Chief Councilor Pei Zan was removed to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Minister of Revenue, and Associate Chief Councilor, was demoted to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 左僕射致仕張濬居長水，王師範之舉兵，濬豫其謀。

translations.literal: The retired Left Vice Director Zhang Jun lived at Changshui; when Wang Shifan raised troops, Jun had foreknowledge of the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Retired Left Vice Director Zhang Jun lived at Changshui and had foreknowledge of Wang Shifan's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠將謀篡奪，恐濬扇動籓鎮，諷張全義使圖之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was about to plot usurpation and feared Jun would stir the frontier commands; he hinted to Zhang Quanyi to scheme against him.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhu Quanzhong planned usurpation, he feared Zhang Jun might stir the provinces and urged Zhang Quanyi to eliminate him.

sentences.zh: 丙申，全義遣牙將楊麟將兵詐為劫盜，圍其墅而殺之。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Quanyi sent guard officer Yang Lin with troops disguised as bandits to surround his villa and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Zhang Quanyi sent Yang Lin with troops disguised as bandits to surround his villa and kill him.

sentences.zh: 永寧縣吏葉彥素為濬所厚，知麟將至，密告濬子格曰：「相公禍不可免，郎君宜自為謀。」

translations.literal: The Yongning county clerk Ye Yansu was favored by Jun; knowing Lin was coming, he secretly told Jun's son Ge: "The chief councilor's disaster cannot be avoided; young master, you should plan for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Yongning clerk Ye Yansu, whom Zhang Jun had favored, learned of the plot and secretly told his son Ge, "Your father's doom is certain—you must save yourself."

sentences.zh: 謂格曰：「汝留則俱死，去則遺種。」

translations.literal: He told Ge: "If you stay you die together; if you go you preserve the line."
translations.idiomatic: He told Ge, "Stay and you die together; leave and the line survives."

sentences.zh: 格哭拜而去，葉彥帥義士三十人送之渡漢而還，格遂自荊南入蜀。

translations.literal: Ge wept, bowed, and left; Ye Yan led thirty righteous men to escort him across the Han and return; Ge then entered Shu from Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ge wept and fled. Ye Yan led thirty men to escort him across the Han, and Ge entered Shu by way of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使劉仁恭習知契丹情偽，常選將練兵，乘秋深入，逾摘星嶺擊之，契丹畏之。

translations.literal: The Lulong military commissioner Liu Rengong was practiced in knowing Khitan truth and falsehood; he often chose generals and trained troops; riding autumn he went deep, crossed Zhaxing Ridge to strike them, and the Khitan feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Lulong commissioner Liu Rengong knew the Khitans well, trained crack troops, and each autumn crossed Zhaxing Ridge to raid them until they feared him.

sentences.zh: 每霜降，仁恭輒遣人焚塞下野草，契丹馬多饑死，常以良馬賂仁恭買牧地。

translations.literal: Whenever frost fell, Rengong would send men to burn the wild grass below the passes; Khitan horses mostly starved to death; they often used fine horses to bribe Rengong to buy pasture land.
translations.idiomatic: Each frost season Liu burned the grass along the passes so Khitan horses starved, and they often bribed him with fine horses for pasture rights.

sentences.zh: 契丹王邪律阿保機遣其妻兄述律阿缽將萬騎寇渝關，仁恭遣其子守光戍平州，守光偽與之和，設幄犒饗於城外，酒酣，伏兵執之以入。

translations.literal: The Khitan king Yelü Abaoji sent his wife's elder brother Shulü Abo with ten thousand horsemen to raid Yuguan; Rengong sent his son Shouguang to garrison Pingzhou; Shouguang pretended peace with them, set tents for a feast outside the city, and when the wine was deep, ambush troops seized them and brought them in.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan king Yelü Abaoji sent his brother-in-law Shulü Abo with ten thousand horsemen against Yuguan. Liu Rengong's son Shouguang garrisoned Pingzhou, feigned friendship, feasted them outside the walls, and seized them when they were drunk.

sentences.zh: 虜眾大哭，契丹以重賂請於仁恭，然後歸之。

translations.literal: The captive host wept greatly; the Khitan used heavy bribes to request them from Rengong, and only then were they returned.
translations.idiomatic: The captives wept loudly. The Khitans paid a heavy ransom before Liu Rengong released them.

sentences.zh: 初，崔胤假朱全忠兵力以誅宦官，全忠既破李茂貞，併吞關中，威震天下，遂有篡奪之志。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Yin borrowed Zhu Quanzhong's military strength to execute the eunuchs; after Quanzhong had broken Li Maozhen and swallowed Guanzhong, his might shook the realm, and he then had usurpation in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cui Yin had used Zhu Quanzhong's armies to destroy the eunuchs. After defeating Li Maozhen and swallowing Guanzhong, Zhu's power shook the realm and he turned toward usurpation.

sentences.zh: 胤懼，與全忠外雖親厚，私心漸異，乃謂全忠曰：「長安密邇茂貞，不可不為守禦之備。

translations.literal: Yin was afraid; outwardly he was close and thick with Quanzhong but inwardly they gradually differed; he then told Quanzhong: "Chang'an is close to Maozhen—we cannot fail to make defensive preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin grew afraid. Outwardly friendly but inwardly estranged, he told Zhu Quanzhong, "Chang'an lies close to Li Maozhen—you need defenses here.

sentences.zh: 六軍十二衛，但有空名，請召募以實之，使公無西顧之憂。」

translations.literal: The Six Armies and Twelve Guards exist only as empty names; I request recruitment to fill them, so that my lord need not worry looking west."
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies and Twelve Guards are hollow names. Recruit to fill them so you need not worry about the west."

sentences.zh: 全忠知其意，曲從之，陰使麾下壯士應募以察其變。

translations.literal: Quanzhong knew his intent, yielded outwardly, and secretly had stalwart men under him enlist to observe his changes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong saw through him, agreed outwardly, and secretly sent his own men to enlist and watch.

sentences.zh: 胤不之知，與鄭元規等繕治兵仗，日夜不息。

translations.literal: Yin did not know this and with Zheng Yuangui and others repaired weapons and armor without rest day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin knew nothing of this and worked day and night with Zheng Yuangui to arm the new troops.

sentences.zh: 及朱友倫死，全忠益疑胤，且欲遷天子都洛，恐胤立異。

translations.literal: When Zhu Youlun died, Quanzhong suspected Yin all the more, and also wished to move the Son of Heaven's capital to Luoyang, fearing Yin would set up opposition.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Youlun's death Zhu Quanzhong suspected Cui Yin all the more and planned to move the capital to Luoyang, fearing Yin would oppose him.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝下之上天祐元年（

translations.literal: On the weightier annals of Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, and Refined Filial Sage—Tianyou year one (
translations.idiomatic: Under the Superior Annals of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang, Tianyou year one (

sentences.zh: 甲子，公元九零四年）

translations.literal: Jiazi, equivalent to the year 904 CE)
translations.idiomatic: 904 CE, year jiazi of the cycle)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，全忠密表司徒兼侍中、判六軍十二衛事、充鹽鐵轉運使、判度支崔胤專權亂國，離間君臣，並其黨刑部尚書兼京兆尹、六軍諸衛副使鄭元規、威遠軍使陳班等，皆請誅之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Quanzhong secretly memorialized that the Minister of Education and Palace Attendant, in charge of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards, acting Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner, and in charge of the budget Cui Yin monopolized power and disturbed the state, estranged sovereign and subjects, and together with his faction—the Minister of Justice and concurrent Jingzhao magistrate and deputy commissioner of the Six Armies guards Zheng Yuangui, the Weiyuan army commissioner Chen Ban, and others—all should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Zhu Quanzhong secretly accused Cui Yin—Minister of Education, Palace Attendant, commander of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards, Salt and Iron commissioner, and budget director—of monopolizing power, sowing discord between emperor and ministers, and named his allies Zheng Yuangui and Chen Ban for execution.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔責授胤太子少傅、分司，貶元規循州司戶，班湊州司戶。

translations.literal: On yisi, an edict demoted Yin to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince with branch-office duties, demoted Yuangui to Xunzhou registrar, and Ban to Couzhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Cui Yin was demoted to Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince at a branch post, Zheng Yuangui to registrar at Xunzhou, and Chen Ban to registrar at Couzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，下詔罪狀胤等。

translations.literal: On bingwu, an edict was issued listing the crimes of Yin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, an edict listed their crimes.

sentences.zh: 以裴樞判左三軍事、充鹽鐵運使，獨孤損判右三軍事、兼判度支。

translations.literal: Pei Shu was put in charge of the Left Three Armies and made Salt and Iron transport commissioner; Dugu Sun was put in charge of the Right Three Armies and concurrently in charge of the budget.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu took the Left Three Armies and Salt and Iron transport; Dugu Sun took the Right Three Armies and the budget.

sentences.zh: 胤所募兵並縱遣之。

translations.literal: All troops Yin had recruited were released and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: All troops Cui Yin had recruited were disbanded.

sentences.zh: 以兵部尚書崔遠為中書侍郎，翰林學士、左拾遺柳璨為右諫議大夫，並同平章事。

translations.literal: Minister of War Cui Yuan was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; Hanlin academician and Left Reminder Liu Can was made Right Remonstrance Grand Master; both were made Associate Chief Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan, Minister of War, became Vice Director of the Secretariat; Liu Can, Hanlin academician and Left Reminder, became Right Remonstrance Grand Master; both were made Associate Chief Councilors.

sentences.zh: 璨，公綽之從孫也。

translations.literal: Can was a grandnephew of Liu Gongchuo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can was a grandnephew of Liu Gongchuo.

sentences.zh: 戊申，朱全忠密令宿衛都指揮使朱友諒以兵圍崔胤第，殺胤及鄭元規、陳班並胤所親厚者數人。

translations.literal: On wushen, Zhu Quanzhong secretly ordered the palace guard overall commander Zhu Youliang to surround Cui Yin's residence with troops and kill Yin, Zheng Yuangui, Chen Ban, and several men Yin had favored.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Zhu Quanzhong secretly ordered palace guard commander Zhu Youliang to surround Cui Yin's house and kill Yin, Zheng Yuangui, Chen Ban, and several of his close associates.

sentences.zh: 初，上在華州，朱全忠屢表請上遷都洛陽，上雖不許，全忠常令東都留守佑國軍節度使張全義繕修宮室。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was at Huazhou, Zhu Quanzhong repeatedly memorialized asking the emperor to move the capital to Luoyang; although the emperor did not agree, Quanzhong often had the eastern capital's acting commissioner and Youguo army military commissioner Zhang Quanyi repair the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at Huazhou, Zhu Quanzhong repeatedly asked him to move the capital to Luoyang. Though the emperor refused, Zhu kept Zhang Quanyi busy repairing the eastern capital's palaces.

sentences.zh: 全忠之克邠州也，質靜難軍節度使楊崇本妻子於河中。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong took Binzhou, he detained the Jingnan army military commissioner Yang Chongben's wife and children at Hezhong as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong took Binzhou, he held Jingnan commissioner Yang Chongben's family hostage at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 崇本妻美，全忠私焉，既而歸之。

translations.literal: Chongben's wife was beautiful; Quanzhong took her privately, then afterward returned her.
translations.idiomatic: Yang's wife was beautiful; Zhu Quanzhong violated her, then sent her back.

sentences.zh: 崇本怒，使謂李茂貞曰：「唐室將滅，父何忍坐視之乎！」

translations.literal: Chongben was enraged and sent someone to tell Li Maozhen: "The house of Tang is about to perish—how can father bear to sit and watch!"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chongben was furious and sent word to Li Maozhen, "The Tang dynasty is dying—how can you sit by and watch?"

sentences.zh: 遂相與連兵侵逼京畿，複姓名為李繼徽。

translations.literal: They then joined forces to press the capital region and restored his surname to Li Jihui.
translations.idiomatic: They then joined armies against the capital, and he restored his original name Li Jihui.

sentences.zh: 己酉，全忠引兵屯河中。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Quanzhong led troops to camp at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Zhu Quanzhong stationed troops at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，上御延喜樓，朱全忠遣牙將寇彥卿奉表，稱邠、歧兵逼畿甸，請上遷都洛陽。

translations.literal: On dingsi, the emperor ascended Yanxi Tower; Zhu Quanzhong sent guard officer Kou Yanqing to present a memorial, saying Bin and Qi troops pressed the capital region and asking the emperor to move the capital to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the emperor went to Yanxi Tower. Zhu Quanzhong sent Kou Yanqing with a memorial claiming Bin and Qi troops threatened the capital and urging removal to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及下樓，裴樞已得全忠移書，促百官東行。

translations.literal: When he came down from the tower, Pei Shu had already received Quanzhong's transfer letter urging the hundred officials to go east.
translations.idiomatic: When he descended, Pei Shu had already received Zhu's letter urging the officials eastward.

sentences.zh: 戊午，驅徙士民，號哭滿路，罵曰：「賊臣崔胤召朱溫來傾覆社稷，使我曹流離至此！」

translations.literal: On wuwu, commoners and officials were driven and displaced; wailing filled the roads; they cursed: "The rebel minister Cui Yin summoned Zhu Wen to overturn the altars of state and drive us to wander here!"
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the people were driven out. The roads rang with wailing: "The traitor Cui Yin summoned Zhu Wen to destroy the realm and drive us into exile!"

sentences.zh: 老幼繈屬，月餘不絕。

translations.literal: Old and young tied together in lines continued for more than a month without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Old and young in endless lines continued for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，車駕發長安，全忠以其將張廷范為御營使，毀長安宮室百司及民間廬舍，取其材，浮渭河而下，長安自此遂丘墟矣。

translations.literal: On renxu, the imperial carriage departed Chang'an; Quanzhong made his general Zhang Tingfan imperial camp commissioner; he destroyed Chang'an's palace halls, government offices, and commoners' dwellings, took their timber, floated it down the Wei River, and from this Chang'an became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the court left Chang'an. Zhu Quanzhong made Zhang Tingfan imperial camp commissioner, demolished the palaces, offices, and houses, rafted the timber down the Wei, and Chang'an became a wasteland.

sentences.zh: 全忠發河南、北諸鎮丁匠數萬，令張全義治東都宮室，江、浙、湖、嶺諸鎮附全忠者，皆輸貨財以助之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong mobilized tens of thousands of laborers and craftsmen from the Henan north and south commands, ordered Zhang Quanyi to manage the eastern capital's palaces, and all circuits along the Yangtze, Zhe, lakes, and Ling ranges that had submitted to Quanzhong sent goods and wealth to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu mobilized tens of thousands of craftsmen from north and south of the Yellow River and had Zhang Quanyi rebuild the eastern capital. Submissive circuits along the Yangtze, Zhe, lakes, and Ling ranges all sent wealth to help.

sentences.zh: 甲子，車駕至華州，民夾道呼萬歲，上泣謂曰：「勿呼萬歲，朕不復為汝主矣！」

translations.literal: On jiazi, the imperial carriage reached Huazhou; the people along the road shouted ten thousand years of life; the emperor wept and told them: "Do not shout ten thousand years—I am no longer your sovereign!"
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the court reached Huazhou. The people shouted long life along the road. The emperor wept and said, "Do not shout long life—I am no longer your lord!"

sentences.zh: 館於興德宮，謂侍臣曰：「鄙語云：『紇干山頭凍殺雀，何不飛去生處樂。」

translations.literal: He lodged at Xingde Palace and told attending officials: "A vulgar saying goes: 'On the peak of Gegan Mountain the sparrow froze to death—why not fly off to where life is pleasant.'"
translations.idiomatic: At Xingde Palace he told his attendants, "A folk saying runs: 'On Gegan Mountain the sparrow froze—why not fly to where life is sweet?'"

sentences.zh: 朕今漂泊，不知竟落何所！」

translations.literal: I now drift in exile and do not know where I shall finally fall!"
translations.idiomatic: I drift in exile and do not know where I shall end!"

sentences.zh: 因泣下沾襟，左右莫能仰視，二月，乙亥，車駕至陝，以東都宮室未成，駐留於陝。

translations.literal: He wept until his robe was soaked; those at his side could not look up; in the second month, on yihai, the imperial carriage reached Shan; because the eastern capital's palaces were not yet finished, he halted at Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He wept until his robe was wet; no one dared look up. In the second month, on yihai, the court reached Shan and halted there because the Luoyang palaces were unfinished.

sentences.zh: 丙子，全忠自河中來朝，上延全忠入寢室見何-{后}-，-{后}-泣曰：「自今大家夫婦委身全忠矣！

translations.literal: On bingzi, Quanzhong came from Hezhong to attend court; the emperor received Quanzhong into the bedchamber to see Empress He; the empress wept and said: "From today the great family's husband and wife entrust themselves to Quanzhong!"
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Zhu Quanzhong came from Hezhong to court. The emperor received him in the bedchamber to see Empress He. The empress wept and said, "From today our household entrusts itself to you!"

sentences.zh: 甲申，立皇子禎為端王，祁為豐王，福為和王，禧為登王，祐為嘉王。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the imperial princes Zhen were made Prince of Duan, Qi Prince of Feng, Fu Prince of He, Xi Prince of Deng, and You Prince of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the princes Zhen, Qi, Fu, Xi, and You were made Princes of Duan, Feng, He, Deng, and Jia.

sentences.zh: 上遣間使以御札告難於王建，建以邛州剌史王宗祐為北路行營指揮使，將兵會鳳翔兵迎車駕，至興平，遇汴兵，不得進而還。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a secret envoy with an imperial note reporting distress to Wang Jian; Jian made Qiongzhou prefect Wang Zongyou commander of the northern route campaigning army, led troops to join Fengxiang forces in welcoming the imperial carriage, reached Xingping, met Bianzhou troops, could not advance, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a secret message to Wang Jian. Wang made Wang Zongyou northern route commander and marched with Fengxiang troops to meet the court, but met Bian troops at Xingping and turned back.

sentences.zh: 建始自用墨制除官，云「俟車駕還長安表聞。」

translations.literal: Jian thereupon began on his own authority to appoint officials by black-edict commission, saying "When the imperial carriage returns to Chang'an I shall memorialize and report."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian then began appointing officials on his own authority, saying he would report when the emperor returned to Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 三月，丁未，以朱全忠兼判左、右神策及六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingwei, Zhu Quanzhong was additionally put in charge of the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and the Six Armies guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingwei, Zhu Quanzhong was placed in charge of the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and the Six Armies guards.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，全忠置酒私第，邀上臨幸。

translations.literal: On guichou, Quanzhong set out wine at his private residence and invited the emperor to visit.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Zhu Quanzhong entertained the emperor at his private residence.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，全忠辭上，先赴洛陽督修宮室。

translations.literal: On yimao, Quanzhong took leave of the emperor and went first to Luoyang to supervise palace repairs.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Zhu Quanzhong took leave and went ahead to Luoyang to supervise the palace work.

sentences.zh: 上與之宴群臣，既罷，上獨留全忠及忠武節度使韓建飲，皇后出，自捧玉卮以飲全忠，晉國夫人可證附上耳語。

translations.literal: The emperor feasted with him and the hundred officials; when it ended the emperor alone kept Quanzhong and the Zhongwu military commissioner Han Jian to drink; the empress came out, herself raised a jade goblet to toast Quanzhong, and the Jin state lady Kezheng leaned close to whisper in his ear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feasted with him and the officials, then kept Zhu Quanzhong and Zhongwu commissioner Han Jian to drink. The empress came out with a jade cup for Zhu, and Lady Kezheng of Jin whispered in his ear.

sentences.zh: 建躡全忠足，全忠以為圖己，不飲，陽醉而出。

translations.literal: Jian trod on Quanzhong's foot; Quanzhong thought he plotted against him, would not drink, and pretended drunkenness and left.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian trod on Zhu's foot. Zhu thought it a plot, refused the cup, feigned drunkenness, and left.

sentences.zh: 全忠奏以長安為佑國軍，以韓建為佑國節度使，以鄭州刺史劉知俊為匡國節度使。

translations.literal: Quanzhong memorialized to make Chang'an the Youguo army, made Han Jian Youguo military commissioner, and made Zhengzhou prefect Liu Zhijun Kuangguo military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong made Chang'an the Youguo army, Han Jian its commissioner, and Zhengzhou prefect Liu Zhijun commissioner of Kuangguo.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，上復遣間使以絹詔告急於王建、楊行密、李克用等，令糾帥籓鎮以圖匡復，曰：「朕至洛陽，則為所幽閉，詔敕皆出其手，朕意不復得通矣！」

translations.literal: On dingsi, the emperor again sent secret envoys with silk edicts reporting urgency to Wang Jian, Yang Xingmi, Li Keyong, and others, ordering them to rally the frontier commands for restoration, saying: "When I reach Luoyang I shall be shut in by them; edicts and orders all come from their hands—my intent can no longer get through!"
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the emperor again sent secret silk edicts to Wang Jian, Yang Xingmi, Li Keyong, and others to rally the provinces for restoration, saying, "When I reach Luoyang I will be imprisoned; edicts will come from Zhu's hand and my will can no longer be heard!"

sentences.zh: 楊行密遣錢傳撩及其婦並顧全武歸錢塘。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent Qian Chuanliao and his wife together with Gu Quanwu back to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent Qian Chuanliao, his wife, and Gu Quanwu back to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 以淮南行軍司馬李神福為鄂岳招討使，復將兵擊杜洪。

translations.literal: The Huainan campaigning marshal Li Shenfu was made E-Yue campaigning commissioner and again led troops to attack Du Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu was made E-Yue campaigning commissioner and again attacked Du Hong.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣使詣行密，請捨鄂岳，復修舊好。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent envoys to Xingmi asking to abandon E-Yue and restore the old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent envoys asking Yang Xingmi to abandon E-Yue and restore friendly relations.

sentences.zh: 行密報曰：「俟天子還長安，然後罷兵修好。」

translations.literal: Xingmi replied: "Wait until the Son of Heaven returns to Chang'an, then cease troops and restore friendship."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi replied, "When the emperor returns to Chang'an, then we can cease hostilities and make peace."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛巳，朱全忠奏洛陽宮室已成，請車駕早發，表章相繼。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinsi, Zhu Quanzhong memorialized that Luoyang's palaces were finished and asked the imperial carriage to depart early; memorials followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinsi, Zhu Quanzhong reported that the Luoyang palaces were ready and urged the court to depart at once in a stream of memorials.

sentences.zh: 上屢遣宮人諭以皇后新產，未任就路，請俟十月東行。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent palace women to explain that the empress had newly given birth and could not yet travel, asking to wait until the tenth month to go east.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly sent palace women to explain that the empress had just given birth and could not travel yet, asking to wait until the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 全忠疑上徘徊俟變，怒甚，謂牙將寇彥卿曰：「汝速至陝，即日促官家發來。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong suspected the emperor lingered awaiting change, was extremely angry, and told guard officer Kou Yanqing: "You hurry to Shan and on this very day urge the imperial household to depart."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong suspected the emperor was stalling for a chance to resist and was furious. He told Kou Yanqing, "Go to Shan at once and bring the court east today."

sentences.zh: 閏月，丁酉，車駕發陝。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on dingyou, the imperial carriage departed Shan.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on dingyou, the court left Shan.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，全忠逆於新安。

translations.literal: On renyin, Quanzhong went out to meet him at Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Zhu Quanzhong met him at Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 上之在陝也，司天監奏：「星氣有變，期在今秋，不利東行。」

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Shan, the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "The stars and vapors have changed; the term falls in this autumn—travel east is unfavorable."
translations.idiomatic: While at Shan, the Directorate of Astronomy reported that the stars foretold misfortune this autumn for an eastern move."

sentences.zh: 故上欲以十月幸洛。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor wished to visit Luoyang in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: That was why the emperor wanted to wait until the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 至是，全忠令醫官許昭遠告醫官使閻祐之、司天監王墀、內都知韋周、晉國夫人可證等謀害元帥，悉收殺之。

translations.literal: At this time Quanzhong had medical officer Xu Zhaoyuan accuse the medical commissioner Yan Youzhi, astronomy director Wang Chi, inner palace director Wei Zhou, Jin state lady Kezheng, and others of plotting to harm the commander-in-chief; all were seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhu Quanzhong had medical officer Xu Zhaoyuan accuse medical commissioner Yan Youzhi, astronomy director Wang Chi, inner director Wei Zhou, Lady Kezheng of Jin, and others of plotting against him; all were arrested and killed.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，上憩於谷水。

translations.literal: On guimao, the emperor rested at Gushui.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the emperor rested at Gushui.

sentences.zh: 自崔胤之死，六軍散亡俱盡，所餘擊球供奉、內園小兒共二百餘人，從上而東。

translations.literal: Since Cui Yin's death the Six Armies had scattered and perished entirely; what remained were more than two hundred ball-playing attendants and inner garden boys who followed the emperor east.
translations.idiomatic: Since Cui Yin's death the Six Armies had vanished. Only about two hundred ball-playing attendants and inner garden boys followed the emperor east.

sentences.zh: 全忠猶忌之，為設食於幄，盡縊殺之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong still feared them, set out food in tents for them, and strangled them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong still feared them, invited them to a meal in the tents, and strangled them all.

sentences.zh: 豫選二百餘人大小相類者，衣其衣服，代之侍衛。

translations.literal: He beforehand chose more than two hundred men of similar size, dressed them in their clothes, and replaced them as guards.
translations.idiomatic: He had already chosen more than two hundred men of similar size, dressed them in the dead men's clothes, and used them as guards.

sentences.zh: 上初不覺，累日乃寤。

translations.literal: At first the emperor did not notice; only after many days did he awaken to it.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor did not notice; only days later did he realize.

sentences.zh: 自是上之左右職掌使令皆全忠之人矣。

translations.literal: From this time all those at the emperor's side who held offices and issued orders were Quanzhong's men.
translations.idiomatic: From then on everyone around the emperor who held office or gave orders was Zhu Quanzhong's man.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，車駕發谷水，入宮，御正殿，受朝賀。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the imperial carriage departed Gushui, entered the palace, ascended the main hall, and received court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the court left Gushui, entered the palace, took the main hall, and received congratulations.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，御光政門，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On yisi, he ascended Guangzheng Gate, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi he went to Guangzheng Gate, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 更命陝州曰興唐府。

translations.literal: Shanzhou was renamed Xingtang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhou was renamed Xingtang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔討李茂貞、楊崇本。

translations.literal: An edict ordered campaigns against Li Maozhen and Yang Chongben.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered campaigns against Li Maozhen and Yang Chongben.

sentences.zh: 戊申，敕內諸司惟留宣徽等九使外，餘皆停廢，仍不以內夫人充使。

translations.literal: On wushen, an edict commanded that among the inner palace offices only the nine commissioners including Xuanhui were retained, the rest all suspended and abolished, and inner palace ladies were still not to serve as commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen an edict retained only nine inner offices including Xuanhui, abolished the rest, and barred inner palace ladies from holding such posts.

sentences.zh: 以蔣玄暉為宣徽南院使兼樞密使，王殷為宣徽北院使兼皇城使，張廷范為金吾將軍、充街使，以韋震為河南尹兼六軍諸衛副使，又征武寧留後朱友恭為左龍武統軍，保大節度使氏叔琮為右龍武統軍，典宿衛，皆全忠之腹心也。

translations.literal: Jiang Xuanhui was made Xuanhui South Court commissioner and concurrently Palace Secretariat commissioner; Wang Yin was made Xuanhui North Court commissioner and concurrently Imperial City commissioner; Zhang Tingfan was made Golden Crow general and street commissioner; Wei Zhen was made Henan magistrate and deputy commissioner of the Six Armies guards; Wuning acting commissioner Zhu Yougong was summoned as Left Dragon Martial commander; Baoda military commissioner Shi Shuzong was made Right Dragon Martial commander in charge of palace guard—all were Quanzhong's trusted intimates.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xuanhui became Xuanhui South Court commissioner and Palace Secretariat commissioner; Wang Yin became North Court commissioner and imperial city commissioner; Zhang Tingfan became Golden Crow general and street commissioner; Wei Zhen became Henan magistrate and deputy Six Armies commissioner; Zhu Yougong was summoned as Left Dragon Martial commander; Shi Shuzong of Baoda became Right Dragon Martial commander—all Zhu Quanzhong's trusted men.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以張全義為天平節度使。

translations.literal: On guichou, Zhang Quanyi was made Tianping military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Zhang Quanyi was made military commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以全忠為護國、宣武，宣義、忠武四鎮節度使

translations.literal: On yimao, Quanzhong was made military commissioner of the four circuits Huguo, Xuanwu, Xuanyi, and Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Zhu Quanzhong was made military commissioner of Huguo, Xuanwu, Xuanyi, and Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 鎮海、鎮東節度使越王錢鏐求封吳越王，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: The Zhenhai and Zhendong military commissioner, King of Yue Qian Liu, requested enfeoffment as King of Wu-Yue; the court did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenhai and Zhendong commissioner Qian Liu, King of Yue, asked to be made King of Wu-Yue; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠為之言於執政，乃更封吳王。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong spoke for him to those in power, and he was then enfeoffed as King of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong intervened with the chief ministers, and Qian Liu was made King of Wu instead.

sentences.zh: 更命魏博曰天雄軍。

translations.literal: Weibo was renamed the Tianxiong army.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo was renamed the Tianxiong army.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，進天雄節度使長沙郡王羅紹威爵鄴王。

translations.literal: On guihai, Tianxiong military commissioner Prince of Changsha Luo Shaowei was advanced to Prince of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Tianxiong commissioner Luo Shaowei, Prince of Changsha, was raised to Prince of Ye.
